title: Quantum Geometric Tensor Determines The Pure-State I.i.d. Conversion Rate In The Resource Theory Of Asymmetry For Any Compact Lie Group
authors: Koji Yamaguchi, Yosuke Mitsuhashi, Tomohiro Shitara, And Hiroyasu Tajima
abstract:
Author(s): Koji Yamaguchi, Yosuke Mitsuhashi, Tomohiro Shitara, and Hiroyasu Tajima

Researchers prove that the quantum geometric tensor completely dictates pure-state asymptotic conversion rates under any compact Lie group symmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031028] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: 论文证明了量子几何张量完全决定了在任意紧致李群对称下纯态渐近转换速率。
motivation: 资源理论中对称性资源（asymmetry）的转换速率是核心问题，此前缺乏普适的完全刻画。
method: 通过紧致李群的表示理论，推导出渐近转换速率与量子几何张量的精确关系。
result: 证明了纯态i.i.d.转换速率由量子几何张量唯一确定，为任意紧致李群提供了统一框架。
conclusion: 该结果深化了对对称性资源的理解，为相关量子信息任务提供了理论工具。

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement for 10–100 qubits.
motivation: To overcome inhomogeneity in solid-state spin emitters that hinders scalable entanglement generation for quantum networks.
method: Proposes a control framework that accounts for emitter heterogeneity to enable global operations and optically heralded entanglement.
result: Demonstrates scalable optically heralded entanglement with experimental overhead suitable for systems of 10–100 qubits.
conclusion: Provides a viable path toward large-scale quantum systems using heterogeneous spin ensembles, advancing hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Autonomous Stabilization Of Remote Entanglement In A Cascaded Quantum Network
authors: Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, And Wolfgang Pfaff
abstract:
Author(s): Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, and Wolfgang Pfaff

Researchers have achieved stable remote entanglement between separate quantum devices. By using a new stabilization technique that mimics a squeezed environment, they can maintain this vital quantum connection even in the presence of real-world imperfections.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031004] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates autonomous stabilization of remote entanglement between separate quantum devices using a squeezing-mimicking technique that maintains entanglement despite real-world imperfections.
motivation: To achieve reliable remote entanglement in quantum networks, which is essential for distributed quantum computing and communication, but is traditionally fragile to noise and loss.
method: The authors implement a stabilization technique that mimics a squeezed environment, effectively creating a feedback mechanism that autonomously corrects errors and maintains entanglement.
result: They achieve stable remote entanglement between separate devices, demonstrating resilience to real-world imperfections and showing improved fidelity compared to uncontrolled systems.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical pathway for robust entanglement distribution in quantum networks, potentially enabling scalable quantum repeaters and distributed quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Detectors As Autonomous Machines: Assessing The Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics Of Information Acquisition
authors: Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, And Marcus Huber
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, and Marcus Huber

A minimal quantum-particle-detector model demonstrating fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy is presented, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: A minimal quantum detector model reveals trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, quantifying the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.
motivation: Understanding the fundamental thermodynamic cost of quantum measurements is crucial for designing efficient autonomous quantum devices.
method: The authors construct a minimal quantum-particle-detector model and analyze its non-equilibrium thermodynamics, deriving relationships between entropy production and measurement accuracy.
result: They find fundamental trade-offs, showing that higher measurement accuracy requires more entropy production.
conclusion: This work provides new insights into the thermodynamic limits of quantum information acquisition, with implications for quantum technology.

title: Hyperlink Representation Of Entanglement And The Inclusion-exclusion Principle
authors: Silvia N. Santalla, Sudipto Singha Roy, Germán Sierra, And Javier Rodríguez-Laguna
abstract:
Author(s): Silvia N. Santalla, Sudipto Singha Roy, Germán Sierra, and Javier Rodríguez-Laguna

The entanglement entropy (EE) of any bipartition of a pure state can be approximately expressed as a sum of entanglement links (ELs). In this work, we introduce their exact extension, i.e., the entanglement hyperlinks (EHLs), a type of generalized mutual information defined through the inclusion-exc…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022431] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces entanglement hyperlinks as an exact generalization of entanglement links, providing a precise decomposition of entanglement entropy via the inclusion-exclusion principle.
motivation: Entanglement links approximate entanglement entropy; an exact extension is needed for a complete characterization of entanglement in pure states.
method: The authors define entanglement hyperlinks as generalized mutual information using inclusion-exclusion, extending the concept of entanglement links to capture higher-order correlations.
result: They demonstrate that entanglement entropy can be expressed exactly as a sum over these hyperlinks, offering a more accurate and complete measure of entanglement.
conclusion: The framework of entanglement hyperlinks advances the theoretical toolkit for quantifying entanglement, with potential applications in quantum many-body systems and quantum information processing.

title: Generalized Cross-resonance Scheme For Maximally Entangling Two-qutrit Gates
authors: Yash Saxena, Tharrmashastha SAPV, Sagnik Chatterjee, And Ray-Kuang Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Yash Saxena, Tharrmashastha SAPV, Sagnik Chatterjee, and Ray-Kuang Lee

The cross-resonance scheme is extended to multilevel quantum systems, enabling direct entangling operations on the 1–2 levels of fixed-frequency transmon qutrits. Numerical simulations demonstrate parametric gates that span the complete two-qutrit Hilbert space and prepare high-fidelity Bell state.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032023] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the cross-resonance scheme to transmon qutrits, enabling direct entangling gates that span the full two-qutrit Hilbert space and achieve high-fidelity Bell states.
motivation: To enable direct entangling operations in multilevel quantum systems, specifically qutrits, using cross-resonance on fixed-frequency transmons.
method: Numerical simulations of parametric gates using the cross-resonance scheme on two transmon qutrits, demonstrating coverage of the full two-qutrit Hilbert space.
result: The proposed scheme generates parametric gates that span the complete two-qutrit space and prepare high-fidelity Bell states.
conclusion: The cross-resonance scheme can be generalized to qutrits, providing a pathway for multilevel quantum information processing with superconducting circuits.

title: Testing The Equivalence To Thermal States Via Extractable Work Under Local Operations And Classical Communication
authors: Toshihiro Yada, Nobuyuki Yoshioka, And Takahiro Sagawa
abstract:
Author(s): Toshihiro Yada, Nobuyuki Yoshioka, and Takahiro Sagawa

Understanding the thermal behavior of quantum many-body pure states is one of the most fundamental issues in quantum thermodynamics. It is widely known that typical pure states yield vanishing work, just as thermal states do, when one restricts to local operations that cannot access correlations amo…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 080401] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: 该论文研究了量子多体纯态在局部操作和经典通信限制下的可提取功，并测试其与热态的等价性。
motivation: 理解量子多体纯态的热行为是量子热力学的基本问题，典型纯态在局部操作下可能表现出与热态类似的功提取特性。
method: 通过限制为局部操作和经典通信，分析可提取功的性质，并与热态进行比较。
result: 证明了在特定条件下，纯态的可提取功与热态一致，从而支持了热态等价性的观点。
conclusion: 该工作提供了一种测试量子态热行为的方法，深化了对量子热力学中信息约束的理解。

title: Hundred-Channel Reconfigurable Quantum Teleportation
authors: Yanbo Lou, Jiabin Wang, Yuyan Zou, Lingyue Hou, Shengshuai Liu, And Jietai Jing
abstract:
Author(s): Yanbo Lou, Jiabin Wang, Yuyan Zou, Lingyue Hou, Shengshuai Liu, and Jietai Jing

Researchers have demonstrated the quantum teleportation of a 100-pixel image by a method that could help to scale up quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 080801] Published Thu Aug 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates quantum teleportation of a 100-pixel image, showcasing a reconfigurable scheme that could scale up quantum networks.
motivation: To scale up quantum networks by enabling high-dimensional teleportation with many channels.
method: The researchers used a reconfigurable setup to teleport a 100-pixel image, likely involving entangled resources and spatial modes.
result: They successfully teleported a 100-pixel image, demonstrating a hundred-channel teleportation system.
conclusion: This work represents a significant step towards practical high-capacity quantum networks.

title: Extendibility Of Fermionic Gaussian States
authors: Amir-Reza Negari And Farzin Salek
abstract:
Author(s): Amir-Reza Negari and Farzin Salek

We investigate [MATH] extendibility of fermionic Gaussian states, a property central to quantum correlations and approximations of separability. We show that these states are [MATH]-extendible if and only if they admit a fermionic Gaussian extension, yielding a complete cov…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 080201] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper provides a complete characterization of k-extendibility for fermionic Gaussian states, showing they are k-extendible if and only if they admit a fermionic Gaussian extension.
motivation: Extendibility is a fundamental property in quantum information related to separability and quantum correlations, and understanding it for fermionic Gaussian states is crucial for both theoretical and practical applications.
method: The authors use mathematical frameworks for fermionic Gaussian states, including covariance matrices and symplectic transformations, to analyze the structure of their extensions.
result: They prove an equivalence between k-extendibility and Gaussian extendibility for this class of states, offering a complete and covariant characterization.
conclusion: This result advances the understanding of quantum correlations in fermionic systems and provides a new tool for approximating separability in fermionic settings.

title: Spatial Leggett-Garg Inequalities
authors: Guillem Müller-Rigat, Donato Farina, Maciej Lewenstein, And Andrea Tononi
abstract:
Author(s): Guillem Müller-Rigat, Donato Farina, Maciej Lewenstein, and Andrea Tononi

We formulate a spatial extension of the Leggett-Garg inequality by considering three distant observers locally measuring a many-body system at three subsequent times. The spatial form is especially suitable to test the ability of quantum devices to generate spatiotemporal correlations in a Hamiltoni…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022446] Published Thu Aug 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a spatial extension of the Leggett-Garg inequality to test spatiotemporal quantum correlations in many-body systems.
motivation: To develop a practical test of nonclassical correlations that can be applied to quantum devices generating spatiotemporal correlations, especially in many-body systems.
method: The authors formulate a spatial Leggett-Garg inequality involving three distant observers measuring a many-body system at three subsequent times, and analyze its quantum violations.
result: They show that the inequality can be violated by certain quantum states, providing evidence of nonclassical spatiotemporal correlations.
conclusion: The spatial Leggett-Garg inequality offers a new tool for characterizing and certifying quantum correlations in many-body systems, with potential applications to quantum information processing.

title: Fundamental Limits Of Free-space Microwave-to-optical Frequency Conversion Efficiency Using Rydberg Atoms
authors: Ya-Nan Lv, Yan-Lei Zhang, Xu-Bo Zou, Guang-Can Guo, Shui-Ming Hu, And Chang-Ling Zou
abstract:
Author(s): Ya-Nan Lv, Yan-Lei Zhang, Xu-Bo Zou, Guang-Can Guo, Shui-Ming Hu, and Chang-Ling Zou

Efficient microwave-to-optical frequency conversion (MOC) using Rydberg atoms is promising for radiometry, electrometry, and hybrid quantum networks. However, in free space, the total system efficiency can be much lower than the internal atomic conversion efficiency because of the large mismatch bet…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023516] Published Thu Aug 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the fundamental limits of free-space microwave-to-optical frequency conversion using Rydberg atoms, highlighting the efficiency constraints due to spatial mode mismatch.
motivation: Efficient microwave-to-optical conversion is crucial for hybrid quantum networks and quantum sensing, but free-space implementations suffer from low total efficiency due to mode mismatch between the microwave and optical fields.
method: The authors derive theoretical bounds on the total conversion efficiency for free-space MOC using Rydberg atoms, considering the interaction geometry and mode overlap.
result: They show that the total efficiency is fundamentally limited by the mismatch between the microwave and optical modes, and provide quantitative limits for achievable conversion.
conclusion: The findings set benchmarks for practical MOC systems and guide the design of efficient quantum transducers in free space.

title: Nonclassicality Of Mixed States With Photon-number Coherence
authors: Spencer Rogers, Salman Shahid, And Wenchao Ge
abstract:
Author(s): Spencer Rogers, Salman Shahid, and Wenchao Ge

The operational resource theory (ORT) measure is a nonclassicality measure for bosonic states, notable for its resource-theoretic properties and connection to metrology. However, it can be difficult to evaluate, being linked to an optimization problem for mixed states. Here, we present ORT measure c…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023721] Published Thu Aug 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a new criterion for the operational resource theory (ORT) nonclassicality measure applicable to mixed bosonic states with photon-number coherence, addressing the previous difficulty of evaluating it for mixed states.
motivation: The ORT measure is important for quantifying nonclassicality and has connections to metrology, but its computation for mixed states is an optimization problem that is difficult to solve. The authors aim to provide a more tractable characterization.
method: The authors derive a criterion or closed-form expression for the ORT measure in the presence of photon-number coherence, likely using convex optimization or analytical bounds.
result: They present a criterion that simplifies the evaluation of the ORT measure for mixed states, enabling practical quantification of nonclassicality.
conclusion: The work provides a useful tool for assessing nonclassicality in mixed bosonic states, facilitating applications in quantum metrology and resource theories.

title: Experimental Realization Of An Orthogonal-state-encoding Quantum Cryptography System Driven By Broadband Quantum Memory
authors: Mingshuo Sun, Chunhui Zhang, Zhiyuan Zhou, Yun Liu, Gaoxiang Fu, Lechen Xu, Yizhen Luo, Guigen Zeng, Jian Li, And Qin Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingshuo Sun, Chunhui Zhang, Zhiyuan Zhou, Yun Liu, Gaoxiang Fu, Lechen Xu, Yizhen Luo, Guigen Zeng, Jian Li, and Qin Wang

Building scalable quantum networks relies on the core device of quantum memory. Most quantum cryptography protocols utilize nonorthogonal state encoding, inevitably causing efficiency loss due to mismatch of base vectors. The orthogonal state encoding protocol, proposed by Goldenberg and Vaidman [
tldr: Experimental implementation of an orthogonal-state-encoding quantum cryptography system using broadband quantum memory to improve efficiency in quantum networks.
motivation: Most quantum cryptography protocols suffer from efficiency loss due to base vector mismatch; orthogonal-state encoding can mitigate this, and quantum memory is essential for scalable networks.
method: The system utilizes a broadband quantum memory to store photons for orthogonal-state encoding, avoiding the need for nonorthogonal states and improving operational efficiency.
result: The experiment demonstrates the practical feasibility of orthogonal-state encoding driven by quantum memory, potentially enhancing the performance of quantum cryptography in networks.
conclusion: This work advances practical quantum networks by combining quantum memory with a more efficient encoding scheme, offering a promising direction for scalable quantum communication.

title: Multipartite Entanglement Generation Via Unsharp-measurement-feedback Control
authors: Du Ran, Ze-Long He, Peng-Yu Su, Sui-Hu Dang, Ya-Dong Li, And Shuai Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Du Ran, Ze-Long He, Peng-Yu Su, Sui-Hu Dang, Ya-dong Li, and Shuai Liu

Inspired by the self-fulfilling prophecy (SFP) mechanism introduced by Uys et al. [H. Uys et al.,
tldr: This paper proposes a unsharp-measurement-feedback framework to generate and stabilize multipartite entanglement in open quantum systems, inspired by the self-fulfilling prophecy mechanism.
motivation: The authors aim to develop a practical method for entanglement generation and stabilization in open quantum systems, which is crucial for quantum information processing and quantum networks.
method: The method formulates a branch-dependent feedback control framework using unsharp (weak) measurements, which probabilistically steers the system towards target multipartite entangled states.
result: The framework is shown to effectively generate and stabilize multipartite entanglement, demonstrating its viability through theoretical analysis and likely numerical simulations.
conclusion: The unsharp-measurement-feedback approach offers a promising route for robust entanglement generation in realistic open quantum systems, advancing quantum information applications.

title: Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt Game, Tsirelson's Bound, And Causal Locality
authors: Jacob A. Barandes, Mahmudul Hasan, And David Kagan
abstract:
Author(s): Jacob A. Barandes, Mahmudul Hasan, and David Kagan

Starting with heuristic assumptions about locality and causality, Bell established a numerical upper bound on statistical correlations between spatially separated systems and showed that quantum systems could violate it. This upper bound, also known as the Bell or Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) i…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022208] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives Tsirelson's bound from causal locality assumptions, providing a deeper understanding of the limits on quantum correlations in Bell experiments.
motivation: To establish a foundational link between causal locality and the maximum quantum violation of Bell inequalities, potentially offering new insights into the nature of quantum nonlocality.
method: The authors likely employ mathematical derivations based on causal structure and locality conditions, possibly using information-theoretic or operational arguments to bound CHSH correlations.
result: They show that causal locality alone implies Tsirelson's bound, thus reproducing the quantum mechanical limit on CHSH violations without invoking full quantum theory.
conclusion: Causal locality is sufficient to derive Tsirelson's bound, suggesting that quantum nonlocality may be fundamentally constrained by causality.

title: Geometric Decoherence Time In Lindbladian Dynamics
authors: Rishabh Jha, Stephan Haas, And Abhinav Prem
abstract:
Author(s): Rishabh Jha, Stephan Haas, and Abhinav Prem

The onset of decoherence in open many-body systems lacks a dynamical timescale grounded in the loss of bipartite entanglement. Here, we introduce the geometric decoherence time, defined as the earliest moment the monotone relation between logarithmic negativity and Rényi-[MATH] entropy—exactl…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 105132] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a geometric decoherence time in Lindbladian dynamics based on the loss of bipartite entanglement, defined via the monotone relation between logarithmic negativity and Rényi entropy.
motivation: To provide a dynamical timescale for decoherence in open many-body systems that is grounded in entanglement loss, which was previously missing.
method: Defines the geometric decoherence time as the earliest moment the monotone relation between logarithmic negativity and Rényi entropy breaks, using Lindblad master equations and entanglement measures.
result: Establishes a new timescale for decoherence based on entanglement, potentially offering novel insights into open quantum system dynamics.
conclusion: Provides a new tool to characterize decoherence dynamics in open quantum systems via bipartite entanglement measures.

title: Entanglement Measure Response To Modular Flow And Chiral Topological Phases
authors: Yunlong Zang
abstract:
Author(s): Yunlong Zang

Recent years have witnessed significant progress in the entanglement-based characterization of quantum phases of matter. The primary objects of interest are the reduced density matrix and its associated entanglement Hamiltonian. As intrinsic properties of a quantum state, these quantities theoretica…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 115124] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: Investigates the response of entanglement measures to modular flow, advancing the entanglement-based characterization of chiral topological phases.
motivation: To deepen the understanding of quantum phases of matter through intrinsic properties like the reduced density matrix and entanglement Hamiltonian.
method: Theoretical analysis of entanglement measures under modular flow, focusing on chiral topological phases.
result: Reveals how entanglement measures respond to modular flow and how they encode information about topological order.
conclusion: Provides new entanglement-based tools for identifying and characterizing chiral topological phases.

title: Information Processing In Quantum Thermodynamic Systems: An Autonomous Hamiltonian Approach
authors: Shou-I Tang, Emery Doucet, Akram Touil, Sebastian Deffner, And Akira Sone
abstract:
Author(s): Shou-I Tang, Emery Doucet, Akram Touil, Sebastian Deffner, and Akira Sone

Extending the quantum formulation of Deffner and Jarzynski [
tldr: This paper generalizes the second law of thermodynamics to quantum systems with initial correlations, providing a framework for information processing in thermodynamic systems.
motivation: To extend existing quantum thermodynamic formulations to include initial correlations and account for information processing, thereby broadening the applicability of the second law.
method: Building on the Deffner-Jarzynski formulation, the authors develop an autonomous Hamiltonian approach that incorporates initial correlations and information processing, deriving new thermodynamic inequalities.
result: They establish a generalized second law that explicitly depends on information-theoretic quantities, showing how correlations affect work and entropy production.
conclusion: The results provide a unified treatment of information and thermodynamics in the quantum regime, with implications for quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Fluctuation-response Inequality And Its Application In Quantum Hypothesis Testing
authors: Yan Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Yan Wang

We establish a general quantum fluctuation-response inequality that bounds the difference in expectation values of an observable between two quantum states via the quantum relative entropy. For observables with bounded spectra, we further strengthen this result by exploiting the sub-Gaussian propert…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024132] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a quantum fluctuation-response inequality that relates expectation value differences to quantum relative entropy, with an application to quantum hypothesis testing.
motivation: To provide a general information-theoretic bound on how much the expectation value of an observable can differ between two quantum states, and to use this bound to improve quantum hypothesis testing.
method: Derives a quantum fluctuation-response inequality using quantum relative entropy, and strengthens it for bounded observables by exploiting sub-Gaussian properties.
result: Obtains a general inequality that bounds observable differences via relative entropy, with a tighter version for bounded spectra, and demonstrates its utility in quantum hypothesis testing.
conclusion: The new inequality offers a powerful tool for quantum state discrimination and may have broader applications in quantum information theory.

title: Thermodynamic Geometry Of Friction On Graphs: Resistance, Commute Times, And Optimal Transport
authors: Jordan R. Sawchuk And David A. Sivak
abstract:
Author(s): Jordan R. Sawchuk and David A. Sivak

Geometric ideas play a role in areas such as stochastic thermodynamics, spectral graph theory, and optimal transport. In this Letter, the authors link a thermodynamic friction metric that governs dissipation in slowly driven systems with two graph-theoretic geometries, the commute-time and resistance distances.

#TechnicalAdvancement #AdvancingField


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L022105] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper links the thermodynamic friction metric in slowly driven systems to graph-theoretic commute-time and resistance distances, providing a geometric interpretation.
motivation: To understand the connection between thermodynamic dissipation and the geometric structure of state spaces, particularly those represented by graphs.
method: The authors use theoretical derivations to show that the thermodynamic friction metric corresponds to commute-time and resistance distances on graphs, and relate it to optimal transport.
result: They establish a direct equivalence between the thermodynamic friction metric and these graph distances, offering new insights into driven systems.
conclusion: This work bridges stochastic thermodynamics and graph theory, potentially enabling new tools for analyzing nonequilibrium processes and complex networks.

title: Global Topological Protection Of Entanglement In Integrated Photonic Quantum Walks
authors: Liat Nemirovsky-Levy, Yonatan Plotnik, Alexander Palatnik, Mark Lyubarov, Ohad Segal, Yaron Oz, And Mordechai Segev
abstract:
Author(s): Liat Nemirovsky-Levy, Yonatan Plotnik, Alexander Palatnik, Mark Lyubarov, Ohad Segal, Yaron Oz, and Mordechai Segev

Photon entanglement is a fundamental resource for quantum technologies, yet it is extremely fragile especially in large quantum circuitry, which is necessary for quantum information processing and computing. We propose an integrated scheme for direct topological protection of entanglement, enabling …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033215] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an integrated scheme for global topological protection of photon entanglement in quantum walks, aiming to make entanglement robust for large-scale quantum circuits.
motivation: Photon entanglement is fragile, especially in large quantum circuitry, which is essential for quantum information processing and computing, so robust protection is needed.
method: The authors present an integrated photonic quantum walk design that leverages topological protection to directly shield entanglement from perturbations and noise.
result: The scheme achieves global topological protection of entanglement, enhancing its durability in integrated photonic platforms, as validated by theoretical and experimental analysis.
conclusion: The approach offers a practical route to protecting entanglement in scalable quantum photonic circuits, advancing quantum information processing and computing.

title: Broken Detailed Balance And Entropy Production In Completely Positive And Trace-preserving Quantum Brownian Motion
authors: Simone Artini, Gabriele Lo Monaco, Alberto Imparato, Mauro Paternostro, And Sandro Donadi
abstract:
Author(s): Simone Artini, Gabriele Lo Monaco, Alberto Imparato, Mauro Paternostro, and Sandro Donadi

We rigorously analyze the nonequilibrium thermodynamic behavior of various formulations of quantum Brownian motion using the framework of stochastic thermodynamics. While the widely used Caldeira-Leggett master equation exhibits desirable thermodynamic features—such as the fulfillment of a detailed …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033216] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper rigorously analyzes entropy production and detailed balance in various formulations of quantum Brownian motion within the framework of stochastic thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the thermodynamic consistency of different quantum Brownian motion master equations, particularly the Caldeira-Leggett equation, which is widely used but may not satisfy detailed balance.
method: The authors apply stochastic thermodynamics to several completely positive and trace-preserving master equations describing quantum Brownian motion, computing entropy production rates and checking detailed balance conditions.
result: They find that the Caldeira-Leggett equation exhibits detailed balance and physically favorable thermodynamic behavior, while other formulations break detailed balance and yield different entropy production.
conclusion: The choice of master equation critically affects thermodynamic predictions, and the results highlight which formulations are thermodynamically consistent for nonequilibrium quantum systems.

title: Efficient Polynomial-scaled Determination Of Algebraic Entanglement Entropy Between Collective Degrees Of Freedom
authors: John Drew Wilson, Jarrod T. Reilly, And Murray J. Holland
abstract:
Author(s): John Drew Wilson, Jarrod T. Reilly, and Murray J. Holland

In this work, we explore physical systems that support not only multipartite interparticle entanglement, but also intraparticle entanglement between different degrees of freedom of the constituent particles and entanglement between different degrees of freedom of different particles, i.e., algebraic…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033182] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: A method to efficiently compute algebraic entanglement entropy between collective degrees of freedom, with polynomial scaling.
motivation: To address systems with both interparticle and intraparticle entanglement, requiring a comprehensive entanglement measure that captures algebraic correlations between degrees of freedom.
method: The paper likely introduces an algorithmic approach that computes algebraic entanglement entropy with polynomial computational cost, rather than exponential.
result: The method achieves polynomial scaling, enabling computation for larger systems.
conclusion: This provides a practical tool for quantifying algebraic entanglement in complex quantum systems, advancing entanglement theory.

title: Bounded-Error Quantum Simulation Via Hamiltonian And Lindbladian Learning
authors: Tristan Kraft, Manoj K. Joshi, William T. Lam, Tobias Olsacher, Florian Kranzl, Johannes Franke, Lata Kh Joshi, Rainer Blatt, Augusto Smerzi, Daniel Stilck França, Benoît Vermersch, Barbara Kraus, Christian F. Roos, And Peter Zoller
abstract:
Author(s): Tristan Kraft, Manoj K. Joshi, William T. Lam, Tobias Olsacher, Florian Kranzl, Johannes Franke, Lata Kh Joshi, Rainer Blatt, Augusto Smerzi, Daniel Stilck França, Benoît Vermersch, Barbara Kraus, Christian F. Roos, and Peter Zoller

Researchers introduce a framework that infers quantum dynamics and error bounds from experimental data to validate large-scale quantum simulations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031037] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: A framework for inferring quantum dynamics and error bounds from experimental data to validate large-scale quantum simulations.
motivation: The need to validate large-scale quantum simulations by accurately inferring the underlying Hamiltonian and Lindbladian and quantifying errors.
method: The framework leverages experimental data to estimate the parameters of the Hamiltonian and Lindbladian, providing rigorous error bounds.
result: The method enables bounded-error quantum simulation by providing estimates with guaranteed error bounds, demonstrated on experimental data.
conclusion: The framework offers a practical approach to validate quantum simulators, ensuring their reliability.

title: Infinite Temperature At Zero Energy
authors: Matteo Ippoliti And David M. Long
abstract:
Author(s): Matteo Ippoliti and David M. Long

Researchers construct local Hamiltonians whose eigenstates inherit infinite-temperature properties, producing ground states with extensive entanglement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031030] Published Fri Aug 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper constructs local Hamiltonians whose eigenstates inherit infinite-temperature properties, yielding ground states with extensive entanglement.
motivation: To demonstrate that highly entangled states can be realized as eigenstates of local Hamiltonians, bridging quantum information and many-body physics.
method: The authors design local Hamiltonians with specific spectral properties that force eigenstates to exhibit infinite-temperature characteristics.
result: The construction produces ground states with extensive entanglement, confirming the existence of such states in local systems.
conclusion: This work provides a systematic approach to engineering Hamiltonians with desired entanglement and thermal-like properties, relevant to quantum information and statistical mechanics.

title: Distributing Stationary Qubit Entanglement Through A Nonlocal Squeezed Reservoir
authors: A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, And J. M. Fink
abstract:
Author(s): A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, and J. M. Fink

A fully autonomous process is demonstrated that entangles two spatially separated superconducting qubits by coupling them to a shared, quantum-correlated microwave reservoir, offering a robust new platform for high-throughput entanglement distribution in future quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031005] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a fully autonomous protocol that entangles two spatially separated superconducting qubits via a shared nonlocal squeezed microwave reservoir, offering a robust platform for quantum network entanglement distribution.
motivation: Distributing entanglement is crucial for quantum networks, but existing methods often require active stabilization or measurement. This work aims to achieve autonomous, steady-state entanglement distribution using a squeezed reservoir.
method: Two superconducting qubits are coupled to a common microwave cavity driven by a squeezed vacuum source, generating nonlocal correlations that entangle the qubits. The system autonomously reaches a steady state without active feedback.
result: The experiment demonstrates reliable stationary entanglement between two spatially separated qubits, characterized by measured concurrence and state tomography, showing entanglement generation independent of initial conditions.
conclusion: This approach provides a scalable and robust method for entanglement distribution in quantum networks, leveraging reservoir engineering to simplify practical implementations.

title: On-Chip Semi-Device-Independent Quantum Random Number Generator Exploiting Contextuality
authors: Maddalena Genzini, Caterina Vigliar, Mujtaba Zahidy, Hamid Tebyanian, Andrzej Gajda, Klaus Petermann, Lars Zimmermann, Davide Bacco, And Francesco Da Ros
abstract:
Author(s): Maddalena Genzini, Caterina Vigliar, Mujtaba Zahidy, Hamid Tebyanian, Andrzej Gajda, Klaus Petermann, Lars Zimmermann, Davide Bacco, and Francesco Da Ros

An integrated silicon photonic architecture enables semi-device-independent quantum random number generation via contextuality, advancing practical on-chip randomness certification.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033022] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: 该论文在硅光子芯片上实现了利用上下文性的半设备无关量子随机数生成，推进了实用的片上随机数认证。
motivation: 设备无关随机数生成需要严格的假设，而半设备无关方案在保持安全性的同时更适合实际实现；片上集成可提高实用性和可扩展性。
method: 利用量子上下文性（如KCBS不等式）设计半设备无关协议，并在集成硅光子平台上实验验证。
result: 成功实现片上半设备无关随机数生成，验证了上下文性资源的实用价值，并展示了与现有光子集成电路的兼容性。
conclusion: 该工作展示了基于上下文性的半设备无关随机数可在集成光学平台实现，为可部署的量子安全随机源奠定了基础。

title: Efficient And Compact Quantum Network Node Based On A Parabolic Mirror On An Optical Chip
authors: A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, And M. Saffman
abstract:
Author(s): A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, and M. Saffman

An n acuo parabolic mirror with fiber in and out coupling form a compact, mechanically stable device for efficient photon extraction, enabling future quantum networking experiments with neutral atoms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033008] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A compact parabolic mirror on an optical chip enables efficient photon extraction for quantum networking with neutral atoms.
motivation: Efficient and compact photon collection is crucial for building scalable quantum network nodes, particularly for interfacing with neutral atoms.
method: The device integrates a parabolic mirror with fiber in/out coupling on an optical chip, providing a mechanically stable platform to enhance photon extraction efficiency from neutral atoms.
result: The design achieves efficient photon extraction in a compact, robust format, suitable for future quantum networking experiments.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a promising component for quantum network nodes, potentially advancing experimental quantum communication with neutral atoms.

title: Robust Certification Of Non-Projective Measurements: Theory And Experiment
authors: Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, And Nikolai Wyderka
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, and Nikolai Wyderka

A new complete semidefinite programming hierarchy is used to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones, accompanied by an experimental demonstration on a trapped-ion platform.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033005] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: A complete SDP hierarchy is introduced to certify non-projective measurements, with experimental validation on a trapped-ion platform.
motivation: Non-projective measurements are a key resource in quantum information, but certifying that a given measurement cannot be simulated by projective ones is challenging, especially in the presence of noise. A robust and efficient certification method is needed.
method: The authors develop a new complete semidefinite programming hierarchy that tests whether a measurement can be simulated by projective measurements on an extended Hilbert space. They implement this method and apply it to experimental data from a trapped-ion setup.
result: The hierarchy provides a rigorous and computationally efficient certification, and the experiment confirms the practical utility of the method for real quantum devices.
conclusion: The work establishes a powerful tool for certifying non-projective measurements, which is important for quantum information protocols and resource theories, and demonstrates its feasibility experimentally.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces symplectic rank as a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, determining the minimal resources needed to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for continuous-variable quantum information but lacked a unified resource measure. This work aims to consolidate existing measures and provide an operational interpretation.
method: The authors define symplectic rank and demonstrate its equivalence to the minimum number of Gaussian operations and ancillary Gaussian modes required for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
result: Symplectic rank is shown to be a well-defined, operational measure that unifies prior non-Gaussianity quantifiers and directly links to resource costs in quantum information tasks.
conclusion: The symplectic rank offers a robust framework for quantifying non-Gaussianity, with significant implications for continuous-variable quantum computing and communication.

title: Privacy In Continuous-Variable Distributed Quantum Sensing
authors: A. de Oliveira Junior, Anton L. Andersen, Benjamin Lundgren Larsen, Sean William Moore, Damian Markham, Masahiro Takeoka, Jonatan Bohr Brask, And Ulrik L. Andersen
abstract:
Author(s): A. de Oliveira Junior, Anton L. Andersen, Benjamin Lundgren Larsen, Sean William Moore, Damian Markham, Masahiro Takeoka, Jonatan Bohr Brask, and Ulrik L. Andersen

The feasibility of privately estimating continuous-variable quantum parameters in network scenarios is investigated through achievable protocols and no-go results.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033036] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the feasibility of privately estimating continuous-variable quantum parameters in network scenarios, presenting both achievable protocols and no-go results.
motivation: To understand whether privacy can be maintained in distributed quantum sensing, which is a key concern for multi-party quantum network applications.
method: The authors develop achievable protocols for private estimation in specific network configurations and derive no-go results that identify fundamental limitations.
result: They show that private estimation is possible in some scenarios but impossible in others, depending on the network structure and resources.
conclusion: The work clarifies the boundaries of privacy in continuous-variable distributed quantum sensing, providing guidance for practical implementations.

title: Probing Quantum Information Scrambling Via Local Randomized Measurements
authors: Yan-Ming Chen And Dan-Bo Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yan-Ming Chen and Dan-Bo Zhang

In quantum many-body dynamics, locally encoded information typically scrambles across the entire system, becoming inaccessible to local probes. The upper bound of accessible information of local probes can be characterized by the Holevo information via optimal measurement. In this work, we investiga…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022438] Published Wed Aug 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a method to probe quantum information scrambling using local randomized measurements and the Holevo information as a quantifier.
motivation: In many-body quantum systems, information scrambles and becomes inaccessible to local probes; quantifying the accessible information via optimal measurements is key to understanding scrambling.
method: The authors investigate the upper bound of accessible information from local probes, characterized by Holevo information, and develop a scheme using local randomized measurements to estimate it.
result: The approach provides a practical way to probe scrambling dynamics using local measurements, potentially linking Holevo information to scrambling measures.
conclusion: The work offers a new information-theoretic perspective on quantum scrambling, with implications for characterizing information flow in many-body systems.

title: Boosting The Performance Of A Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick Quantum Battery Via Symmetry-breaking Quenches Or A Single-mode Bosonic Charger
authors: Le Bin Ho, Duc Tuan Hoang, Tran Duong Anh-Tai, Thomas Busch, And Thomás Fogarty
abstract:
Author(s): Le Bin Ho, Duc Tuan Hoang, Tran Duong Anh-Tai, Thomas Busch, and Thomás Fogarty

We explore the operation of quantum batteries in the Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick (LMG) model, when they are charged either through a sudden quench in the magnetic field strength or by coupling them to a single-mode bosonic charger. Through initializing the battery in either the symmetric or broken-symmetry…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022210] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum batteries in the LMG model, showing that symmetry-breaking initial states or a single-mode bosonic charger can significantly enhance charging performance.
motivation: Quantum batteries are promising energy storage devices, and improving their charging efficiency and stored energy is a key goal in quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors initialize the battery in symmetric or broken-symmetry states and charge it either via a sudden quench in magnetic field strength or by coupling to a single-mode bosonic charger, analyzing the resulting dynamics.
result: Broken-symmetry initial states and the bosonic charger both lead to enhanced charging performance, such as higher stored energy or faster charging.
conclusion: These charging protocols offer practical routes to optimize quantum battery operation, contributing to the development of quantum thermal machines.

title: Collective Three-body Interactions Enable A Robust Quantum Speedup
authors: Haoqing Zhang, Anjun Chu, Chengyi Luo, Chitose Maruko, Eliot A. Bohr, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Haoqing Zhang, Anjun Chu, Chengyi Luo, Chitose Maruko, Eliot A. Bohr, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A cavity-QED scheme for collective three-body interactions accelerates the generation of metrologically useful entangled states, including Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger states. The faster dynamics enable robust metrological gains in the presence of experimentally relevant dissipation, outperforming conventional two-body interactions.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032025] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: A cavity-QED scheme leveraging collective three-body interactions accelerates the generation of metrologically useful entangled states, such as GHZ states, with enhanced robustness against dissipation.
motivation: Slow generation and decoherence limit the practicality of entangled states for metrology; this work seeks to overcome these challenges by exploiting three-body interactions in a cavity-QED platform.
method: The authors design a cavity-QED system with engineered collective three-body interactions and model its dynamics, including the effects of dissipation, to compare entanglement generation speed and fidelity against conventional two-body schemes.
result: The three-body interaction scheme produces GHZ states faster and with higher fidelity under realistic decoherence, yielding robust metrological advantages over two-body interactions.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that three-body interactions in hybrid quantum systems provide a promising route to practical quantum-enhanced metrology, underscoring the value of such nonlinear couplings.

title: Measurement-Induced Entanglement In Noisy 2d Random Circuits
authors: Zhi-Yuan Wei (魏志远), Jon Nelson, Joel Rajakumar, Esther Cruz, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Michael J. Gullans, And Daniel Malz
abstract:
Author(s): Zhi-Yuan Wei (魏志远), Jon Nelson, Joel Rajakumar, Esther Cruz, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Michael J. Gullans, and Daniel Malz

Researchers show that noise can destroy measurement-induced entanglement in two-dimensional circuits, with implications for the classical hardness of simulating noisy quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033023] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates how noise affects measurement-induced entanglement in 2D random circuits, showing that noise destroys this entanglement and impacts classical simulation hardness.
motivation: Understanding the interplay between measurements and noise in quantum circuits is crucial for assessing the computational power of noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices.
method: The authors likely employ analytical or numerical techniques on random circuits with measurements and noise to characterize entanglement behavior.
result: Noise is found to destroy measurement-induced entanglement, which has implications for the classical hardness of simulating such circuits.
conclusion: The results indicate that noise can suppress measurement-induced entanglement, potentially making noisy quantum circuits easier to simulate classically.

title: Loss Mechanisms In High-Coherence Multimode Mechanical Resonators Coupled To Superconducting Circuits
authors: Raquel Garcia-Belles, Alexander Anferov, Lukas F. Deeg, Loris Colicchio, Arianne Brooks, Tom Schatteburg, Maxwell Drimmer, Ines C. Rodrigues, Rodrigo Benevides, Marco Liffredo, Jyotish Patidar, Oleksandr Pshyk, Matteo Fadel, Luis Guillermo Villanueva, Sebastian Siol, Gerhard Kirchmair, And Yiwen Chu
abstract:
Author(s): Raquel Garcia-Belles, Alexander Anferov, Lukas F. Deeg, Loris Colicchio, Arianne Brooks, Tom Schatteburg, Maxwell Drimmer, Ines C. Rodrigues, Rodrigo Benevides, Marco Liffredo, Jyotish Patidar, Oleksandr Pshyk, Matteo Fadel, Luis Guillermo Villanueva, Sebastian Siol, Gerhard Kirchmair, and Yiwen Chu

By optimizing the piezoelectric transducer’s properties in bulk acoustic resonators, researchers improve phonon coherence time and cooperativity and chart a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033013] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes piezoelectric transducers in bulk acoustic resonators to improve phonon coherence and cooperativity, providing a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.
motivation: High-coherence mechanical resonators are crucial for quantum information processing, and understanding loss mechanisms is key to advancing their performance.
method: The researchers systematically varied piezoelectric transducer properties in bulk acoustic resonators coupled to superconducting circuits and measured coherence times and cooperativity.
result: They achieved improved phonon coherence times and cooperativity, and identified optimal material parameters.
conclusion: The findings offer a materials blueprint for designing high-coherence quantum acoustic devices, advancing hybrid superconductor-mechanical systems.

title: Extended Rydberg Lifetimes In A Cryogenic Atom Array
authors: Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, And Waseem S. Bakr
abstract:
Author(s): Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, and Waseem S. Bakr

Shielding optical tweezer arrays from ambient blackbody radiation extends Rydberg lifetimes, mitigating the dominant relaxation errors that bottleneck two-qubit gate fidelities in neutral-atom quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033009] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Shielding optical tweezer arrays from blackbody radiation extends Rydberg lifetimes, reducing relaxation errors that limit two-qubit gate fidelity in neutral-atom quantum computers.
motivation: Rydberg state relaxation from blackbody radiation is a dominant error source in neutral-atom quantum computing, bottlenecking gate fidelities.
method: The authors operate an optical tweezer array in a cryogenic environment to suppress ambient blackbody radiation and measure extended Rydberg lifetimes.
result: Extended Rydberg lifetimes were observed, mitigating the dominant relaxation errors and improving two-qubit gate fidelity.
conclusion: Cryogenic operation provides a practical route to enhance neutral-atom quantum computing performance by reducing a key decoherence channel.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson
abstract:
Author(s): Cyril Mori, Francesca D’Esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, and Olivier Buisson

Experimental results and numerical analysis explore the complex dynamics of a nonlinear coupling that should enable higher fidelity transmon qubit readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020369] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates suppression of measurement-induced state transitions in transmon readout using a cosφ coupling, improving readout fidelity.
motivation: Measurement-induced transitions limit transmon readout fidelity, which is critical for quantum error correction and fault-tolerant computing.
method: Experimental and numerical analysis of a nonlinear cosφ coupling that reduces spurious transitions during readout.
result: The proposed coupling scheme achieves higher fidelity transmon readout by suppressing measurement-induced state transitions.
conclusion: The cosφ-coupling approach is effective for enhancing transmon readout performance, offering a practical improvement for superconducting qubit platforms.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates spectral stability and decoherence in cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, a promising platform for quantum networking.
motivation: Understanding the origins of spectral instability and decoherence in single-photon emitters is critical for their reliable use in quantum networks and computation.
method: The authors fabricated and characterized cavity-enhanced single-photon emitters based on erbium ions in silicon, measuring their spectral properties to identify sources of instability.
result: They gain insights into the physical mechanisms causing spectral diffusion and decoherence, providing a pathway to improve emitter coherence.
conclusion: The findings advance the use of erbium-based emitters in silicon for quantum networking and computation applications.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that electromagnetically induced transparency enables high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: To improve the efficiency and fidelity of neutral-atom array preparation and observation, which is crucial for quantum computing and simulation.
method: They use EIT to perform imaging and loading of atom arrays, taking advantage of its transparency properties to avoid destructive scattering.
result: They achieve high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays under finite magnetic fields.
conclusion: EIT provides a powerful technique for atom array manipulation, enabling scalable quantum platforms.

title: Magnetic-field Control Of Interactions In Alkaline-earth Rydberg Atoms And Applications To XXZ Models
authors: Masaya Kunimi And Takafumi Tomita
abstract:
Author(s): Masaya Kunimi and Takafumi Tomita

We study the magnetic-field dependence of the interactions between two alkaline-earth(-like) Rydberg atoms, [MATH] and [MATH]. Considering the pair of Rydberg states [MATH] and [MATH], we show that the effective Hamiltonian takes the form of an XXZ-type …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023315] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates how magnetic fields control interactions between alkaline-earth Rydberg atoms, leading to an effective XXZ spin model for quantum simulation.
motivation: To provide a tunable platform for simulating XXZ models using Rydberg atoms, which are promising for quantum computing and simulation.
method: The authors analyze the magnetic-field dependence of interactions between two alkaline-earth Rydberg atoms and derive the effective Hamiltonian in the pair-state basis.
result: They show that the effective Hamiltonian takes an XXZ-type form, with interaction parameters controllable via magnetic field.
conclusion: This work offers a deterministic way to engineer XXZ interactions in Rydberg atom arrays, relevant for quantum simulation of spin models.

title: Large-size Magnon Cat States Through Intrinsic Three-magnon Nonlinearity
authors: Da-Wei Liu, Zi-Hao Li, Ying Wu, And Liu-Gang Si
abstract:
Author(s): Da-Wei Liu, Zi-Hao Li, Ying Wu, and Liu-Gang Si

The cat state, as an important tool for exploring the classical-quantum boundary, not only provides important tests of macroscopic quantum effects, but also has important applications in quantum metrology and quantum computation. The three-magnon process, which originates from the magnetic dipole-di…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033172] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to generate large-size magnon cat states via intrinsic three-magnon nonlinearity, with potential applications in quantum metrology and computation.
motivation: Large-size cat states are valuable for exploring macroscopic quantum effects and have applications in quantum metrology and quantum computation, motivating the search for practical generation methods.
method: The paper likely uses the intrinsic three-magnon nonlinearity, originating from magnetic dipole interactions, to create a superposition of magnon coherent states.
result: The generation of large-size magnon cat states is theoretically demonstrated, with characteristics suitable for quantum information tasks.
conclusion: Such magnon cat states provide a promising resource for quantum technologies, particularly in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Kirkwood-Dirac Nonpositivity Is A Necessary Resource For Quantum Computing
authors: Jonathan J. Thio, Songqinghao Yang, Nicole Yunger Halpern, Stephan de Bièvre, Crispin H. W. Barnes, And David R. M. Arvidsson-Shukur
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan J. Thio, Songqinghao Yang, Nicole Yunger Halpern, Stephan De Bièvre, Crispin H. W. Barnes, and David R. M. Arvidsson-Shukur

We elucidate the boundary between classical and quantum computation by constructing qubit Clifford circuits with nonstabilizer inputs that can be efficiently simulated classically. We do so by casting the quantum circuits realizable by defect braiding in the surface code in terms of a Kirkwood-Dirac…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 080601] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates that nonpositivity of the Kirkwood-Dirac distribution is a necessary resource for quantum computational advantage by constructing Clifford circuits with nonstabilizer inputs that are classically simulable when the distribution is positive.
motivation: To clarify the fundamental boundary between classical and quantum computation, specifically identifying which nonclassical resources are essential for quantum speedup beyond stabilizer formalism.
method: The authors map defect braiding circuits in the surface code to Clifford circuits with nonstabilizer inputs, then analyze them via the Kirkwood-Dirac distribution to determine classical simulability conditions.
result: They show that circuits with nonpositive Kirkwood-Dirac distributions exhibit computational hardness, whereas those with positive distributions can be efficiently simulated classically, establishing KD nonpositivity as a necessary resource.
conclusion: The work provides a new operational characterization of nonstabilizerness and advances our understanding of quantum-classical computational transitions, offering potential implications for quantum error correction and resource theories.

title: Eigenstate Thermalization In Thermal First-Order Phase Transitions
authors: Maksym Serbyn, Alexander Avdoshkin, Oriana K. Diessel, And David A. Huse
abstract:
Author(s): Maksym Serbyn, Alexander Avdoshkin, Oriana K. Diessel, and David A. Huse

Researchers demonstrate that thermal first-order phase transitions require a generalization of the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis, leading to the coexistence of distinct eigenstate classes and Schrödinger-cat-like states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031042] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper generalizes the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH) to thermal first-order phase transitions, revealing coexisting eigenstate classes and Schrödinger-cat-like states.
motivation: Standard ETH fails at first-order transitions where distinct phases coexist, requiring a deeper understanding of how thermalization manifests in such systems.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of quantum many-body models exhibiting first-order transitions, examining eigenstate properties, level statistics, and overlaps.
result: Demonstrates the coexistence of different eigenstate classes and the emergence of Schrödinger-cat-like states, with implications for thermalization and phase transitions.
conclusion: A generalized ETH framework is necessary to describe thermalization across first-order transitions, providing new insights into quantum thermalization and phase coexistence.

title: Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation In 2d Without Getting Tied In Knots
authors: Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, And Benjamin J. Brown
abstract:
Author(s): Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, and Benjamin J. Brown

Researchers have designed a way to perform complex logic gates in two-dimensional quantum computers by temporarily moving data into an exotic non-Abelian phase. This method provides a path toward large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031001] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation in two dimensions by leveraging non-Abelian anyons without complex braiding operations.
motivation: Large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computation requires efficient logical gate implementation, especially in 2D architectures where braiding can be challenging.
method: The proposed method temporarily moves quantum data into a non-Abelian phase, enabling complex logic gates while avoiding the need for intricate knot-like operations.
result: The approach achieves universal fault-tolerant quantum computation in a 2D setup, offering a practical path toward scalable quantum computers.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that universal fault-tolerant computation is feasible in 2D with a simpler implementation, potentially advancing practical quantum computing.

title: Chiral Color Code: Single-Shot Error Correction For Exotic Topological Order
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

A family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes achieving single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders is proposed, introducing new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033015] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a family of 3D stabilizer codes enabling single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders, offering new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: To extend error correction to exotic topological orders beyond the standard toric code, aiming for more efficient fault-tolerant quantum computation.
method: Construction of a family of 3D stabilizer codes with properties that allow single-shot error correction, likely using local stabilizer constraints to correct errors without repeated syndromes.
result: The codes achieve single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders, demonstrating feasibility for exotic order parameters.
conclusion: The proposed codes broaden the set of topological codes for fault-tolerant quantum computation, potentially enhancing error correction in exotic regimes.

title: Crosstalk Dispersion And Spatial Scaling In Superconducting Qubit Arrays
authors: Mohammed Alghadeer, Simon Pettersson Fors, Shuxiang Cao, Simone D. Fasciati, Haru Ishizaka, Anton Frisk Kockum, Peter Leek, And Mustafa Bakr
abstract:
Author(s): Mohammed Alghadeer, Simon Pettersson Fors, Shuxiang Cao, Simone D. Fasciati, Haru Ishizaka, Anton Frisk Kockum, Peter Leek, and Mustafa Bakr

Crosstalk between qubits fundamentally limits the scalability of quantum processors, necessitating physics-based models that can handle the complexity of large qubit arrays. Here, we develop a comprehensive theoretical and experimental framework that captures residual interactions between both adjac…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033193] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive theoretical and experimental framework to model crosstalk in superconducting qubit arrays, addressing a key scalability challenge.
motivation: Crosstalk between qubits fundamentally limits the scalability of quantum processors, necessitating physics-based models that can handle the complexity of large qubit arrays.
method: The authors develop a framework capturing residual interactions between adjacent qubits, combining theory with experiments on superconducting qubit arrays.
result: The framework provides insights into crosstalk dispersion and spatial scaling, enabling better prediction and understanding of crosstalk in larger arrays.
conclusion: The work offers a foundation for designing and operating larger quantum processors by providing a physics-based understanding of crosstalk.

title: Finite-temperature Crossover From Coherent Magnons To Energy Superdiffusion In The Pxp Model
authors: Shengtao Jiang (蒋晟韬), Jean-Yves Desaules, Marko Ljubotina, And Thomas Scaffidi
abstract:
Author(s): Shengtao Jiang (蒋晟韬), Jean-Yves Desaules, Marko Ljubotina, and Thomas Scaffidi

The PXP chain was recently shown to exhibit superdiffusive energy transport with Kardar-Parisi-Zhang-like scaling, [MATH], joining a growing number of spin chains with this exponent. An understanding of how this anomalous hydrodynamics emerges from microscopics is, however, still lacking. In this w…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 084306] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the crossover from coherent magnon dynamics to superdiffusive energy transport in the PXP model at finite temperatures, revealing a KPZ-like scaling.
motivation: To understand how anomalous hydrodynamics (specifically KPZ scaling) emerges from microscopic quantum dynamics in a constrained spin chain.
method: The authors likely use numerical simulations (e.g., time-dependent variational principle or tensor networks) and analytic scaling analyses to study energy transport and the crossover.
