authors: Leonardo A. M. Souza, Olimpio P. de Sá Neto, Enrico Russo, Rosario Lo Franco, And Gerardo Adesso
abstract:
Author(s): Leonardo A. M. Souza, Olimpio P. de Sá Neto, Enrico Russo, Rosario Lo Franco, and Gerardo Adesso

We develop a comprehensive quantum estimation framework to quantify how precisely gravitationally induced decoherence can be inferred in optomechanical systems, using single-mode Gaussian probe states. Our approach combines a microscopic description of the gravitational diffusion mechanism with quan…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022442] Published Thu Aug 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a quantum estimation framework to quantify how precisely gravitationally induced decoherence can be inferred in optomechanical systems using Gaussian probe states.
motivation: The goal is to assess the observability of gravitational decoherence in optomechanical setups, which is relevant for testing fundamental physics and quantum-gravity effects.
method: The authors combine a microscopic model of gravitational diffusion with quantum estimation theory, using single-mode Gaussian states as probes, to compute bounds on estimation precision.
result: They provide quantitative estimates for how accurately gravitational decoherence can be measured, potentially enabling experimental detection in feasible optomechanical platforms.
conclusion: The framework offers a practical avenue for inferring gravitational decoherence, bridging quantum optics and gravity, and may guide future experiments in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Sub-Riemannian Lift Advantage In Quantum Control
authors: Ryan Choi, Vwani Roychowdhury, And Louis-S. Bouchard
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Choi, Vwani Roychowdhury, and Louis-S. Bouchard

We present an extended-algebra (EA) control workflow for fixed-horizon, bounded-amplitude quantum control. The method optimizes a state-transfer trajectory in a polynomial EA, projects the optimized lifted trajectory to native physical controls using a budgeted dictionary of product-formula approxim…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022441] Published Wed Aug 19, 2026.
tldr: 该论文提出了一种基于扩展代数的量子控制工作流，利用子黎曼提升来优化固定时域、有界幅度的量子态转移。
motivation: 量子控制是量子信息处理的关键，但现有方法在固定时域和幅度限制下优化效率有限。
method: 提出了EA控制工作流，在多项式EA中优化态转移轨迹，然后通过预算字典投影到原生物理控制。
result: 证明了子黎曼提升在量子控制中的优势，可能提升控制保真度。
conclusion: 该工作为量子控制提供了新的理论工具，有望在量子计算和量子通信中得到应用。

title: Information Geometry Of Bosonic Gaussian Thermal States
authors: Zixin Huang And Mark M. Wilde
abstract:
Author(s): Zixin Huang and Mark M. Wilde

Bosonic Gaussian thermal states form a fundamental class of states in quantum information science. This paper explores the information geometry of these states, focusing on characterizing the distance between two nearby states and the geometry induced by a parametrization in terms of their mean vect…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022437] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes the information geometry of bosonic Gaussian thermal states by examining distances between nearby states and the geometry of their parameter space.
motivation: Understanding the geometric structure of quantum states is crucial for quantum estimation theory and metrology. Gaussian thermal states are fundamental and ubiquitous in quantum optics.
method: The authors likely employ techniques from quantum information geometry, using the quantum Fisher information and Bures distance, applied to the covariance matrix parameterization of Gaussian states.
result: They derive explicit expressions for the quantum Fisher information metric and possibly show that the geometry is flat or has curvature related to temperature and squeezing.
conclusion: The results provide a deeper understanding of the statistical distinguishability of Gaussian thermal states, with implications for quantum metrology and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Classical Simulation Of Noisy Quantum Circuits Via Locally Entanglement-optimal Unravelings
authors: Simon Cichy, Paul K. Faehrmann, Lennart Bittel, Jens Eisert, And Hakop Pashayan
abstract:
Author(s): Simon Cichy, Paul K. Faehrmann, Lennart Bittel, Jens Eisert, and Hakop Pashayan

Classical simulations of noisy quantum circuits are instrumental to our understanding of the behavior of real-world quantum systems and the identification of regimes where one expects quantum advantage. In this work, we present a highly parallelizable tensor-network-based classical algorithm, equipp…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022430] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a parallelizable tensor-network algorithm for classically simulating noisy quantum circuits using locally entanglement-optimal unravelings, aiding in the identification of quantum advantage.
motivation: To better understand the behavior of noisy quantum circuits and determine the regimes where quantum advantage is expected.
method: The algorithm employs tensor networks and locally entanglement-optimal unravelings to simulate the dynamics of noisy quantum circuits in a highly parallelizable manner.
result: The method enables efficient classical simulation of certain noisy circuits, providing a tool for benchmarking quantum devices.
conclusion: This work offers a powerful classical simulation technique that helps assess the potential for quantum advantage in real-world systems.

title: Calibration-conditioned Featurewise Linear Modulation Decoders For Low-latency Decoding Of Quantum Error Correction Evaluated On Ibm Repetition-code Experiments
authors: Samuel Stein, Shuwen Kan, Chenxu Liu, Adrian Harkness, Sean Garner, Zefan Du, Yufei Ding, Ying Mao, And Ang Li
abstract:
Author(s): Samuel Stein, Shuwen Kan, Chenxu Liu, Adrian Harkness, Sean Garner, Zefan Du, Yufei Ding, Ying Mao, and Ang Li

Real-time decoding of quantum error correction is essential for enabling fault-tolerant quantum computation. A practical decoder must operate with high accuracy at low latency, while remaining robust to spatial and temporal variations in hardware noise. We introduce a hardware-conditioned neural dec…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033194] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a calibration-conditioned neural decoder for quantum error correction that achieves low-latency decoding robust to hardware variations, evaluated on IBM repetition-code experiments.
motivation: Real-time decoding of quantum error correction is critical for fault-tolerant quantum computing, requiring high accuracy at low latency while being robust to spatial and temporal noise variations.
method: The authors propose a decoder based on featurewise linear modulation, conditioned on hardware calibration data, to adapt to varying noise conditions in real time.
result: The decoder demonstrates improved accuracy and latency compared to standard decoders in experiments on IBM's repetition-code hardware, showing robustness to calibration drift.
conclusion: The approach offers a practical solution for low-latency, hardware-aware decoding, advancing the feasibility of fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, enabling identification of unknown spin environments and real-time adaptive measurements.
motivation: High-dimensional quantum systems present challenges for scalable and fast estimation, which is critical for characterizing spin environments and enabling adaptive strategies.
method: The framework uses variational Bayesian inference to approximate posterior distributions over quantum states and models, allowing efficient model selection and parameter estimation.
result: The method accurately identifies unknown spin environments and supports real-time adaptive measurement strategies, demonstrated in experiments.
conclusion: This work provides a powerful tool for quantum system characterization, with implications for quantum sensing and quantum information processing.

title: Multiple Phases In ${\mathrm{K}}_{2}{\mathrm{Cr}}_{3}{\mathrm{As}}_{3}$: A Playground For Manipulating Topological Superconductivity
authors: Seigo Ogawa, Tomoki Miyoshi, Saki Uchida, Kazuaki Matano, Shinji Kawasaki, Yoshihiko Inada, And Guo-Qing Zheng
abstract:
Author(s): Seigo Ogawa, Tomoki Miyoshi, Saki Uchida, Kazuaki Matano, Shinji Kawasaki, Yoshihiko Inada, and Guo-qing Zheng

Researchers have made the first definitive measurements of an elusive superconducting state.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 086003] Published Wed Aug 19, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the first definitive measurements of an elusive superconducting state in K2Cr3As3, revealing multiple phases that allow manipulation of topological superconductivity.
motivation: To understand and control topological superconductivity, which is of interest for quantum computing applications.
method: Experimental measurements on K2Cr3As3 samples to characterize the superconducting phases.
result: Evidence for multiple superconducting phases relevant to topological superconductivity.
conclusion: K2Cr3As3 serves as a promising platform for studying and manipulating topological superconductivity.

title: Anomalous Hydrodynamic Fluctuations In The Quantum Xxz Spin Chain
authors: Takato Yoshimura, Žiga Krajnik, Alvise Bastianello, And Enej Ilievski
abstract:
Author(s): Takato Yoshimura, Žiga Krajnik, Alvise Bastianello, and Enej Ilievski

The quantum XXZ spin-[MATH] chain features non-Gaussian spin current fluctuations in the regime of easy-axis anisotropy. Using ballistic macroscopic fluctuation theory, we derive the exact asymptotic probability distribution of typical spin-current fluctuations in thermal equilibrium at zero average …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 086302] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives the exact asymptotic probability distribution of spin current fluctuations in the quantum XXZ spin chain using ballistic macroscopic fluctuation theory, revealing non-Gaussian behavior.
motivation: To understand anomalous transport and fluctuations in integrable quantum systems, particularly the non-Gaussian statistics of spin currents.
method: The authors employ ballistic macroscopic fluctuation theory to analyze typical spin-current fluctuations in thermal equilibrium at zero average current, obtaining exact asymptotic distributions.
result: They find that the spin current fluctuations are non-Gaussian and derive the exact probability distribution, which is a novel result for this integrable model.
conclusion: This work provides a complete characterization of spin current fluctuations in the XXZ chain, advancing the understanding of non-equilibrium dynamics and fluctuations in integrable many-body systems.

title: Infinitesimal Environmental Dust As A Photonic Bath At Infinity
authors: Gaomin Tang, Yuhua Ren, And Jian-Sheng Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Gaomin Tang, Yuhua Ren, and Jian-Sheng Wang

In far-field thermal radiation, electromagnetic waves emitted by an object propagate to infinity, requiring the far region to be modeled as an effective thermal bath. This bath was proposed as infinitesimal environmental “dust,” but explicit calculations with such distributed dust involve integrals …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023517] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to model far-field thermal radiation as an effective photonic bath using infinitesimal environmental dust, simplifying heat transfer calculations.
motivation: In far-field thermal radiation, the far region must be treated as an effective thermal bath, but explicit calculations with distributed dust involve complex integrals.
method: The authors introduce infinitesimal environmental dust as a model for the photonic bath and perform explicit calculations addressing the integrals.
result: They present a tractable formulation for the photonic bath at infinity, enabling easier modeling of far-field thermal radiation.
conclusion: This provides a refined theoretical framework for far-field thermal radiation, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and heat transfer.

title: Connection Between The Liouvillian Gap Closing And Bound States In The Continuum: Diverse Dynamics In A Giant-atom Waveguide Qed Setup
authors: Hongwei Yu, Mingzhu Weng, Zhihai Wang, And Jin Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Hongwei Yu, Mingzhu Weng, Zhihai Wang, and Jin Wang

In open quantum systems, reduced dynamics is commonly described by a master equation, whose Liouvillian gap closing (LGC) typically signals the emergence of decoherence-free subspace. By contrast, the dynamics of the full system-environment compound is governed by the underlying Hamiltonian spectrum…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023722] Published Thu Aug 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper explores the relationship between Liouvillian gap closing and bound states in the continuum in a giant-atom waveguide QED setup, uncovering diverse dynamic behaviors in open quantum systems.
motivation: Understanding when decoherence-free subspaces emerge is crucial for robust quantum information processing; the connection to bound states in the continuum may provide new physical insights.
method: The authors analyze an open quantum system described by a master equation and compare the Liouvillian gap closing with the spectrum of the full system-environment Hamiltonian, focusing on a giant-atom waveguide QED configuration.
result: They find that the Liouvillian gap closing can be associated with the presence of bound states in the continuum, leading to diverse dynamics that deviate from purely dissipative behavior.
conclusion: The study establishes a deeper link between open-system spectral properties and Hamiltonian spectrum, which could inform the design of decoherence-free subspaces and quantum memories.

title: Nonstationary Hierarchical Equations Of Motion In Complex Time
authors: Mauro Cirio And Pengfei Liang
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro Cirio and Pengfei Liang

We present the formal derivation of a set of hierarchical equations of motion (HEOM) to compute system and environmental correlation functions in terms of a nonstationary underlying dynamics in complex time. This corresponds to partitioning the global validity of the HEOM spectral ansatz into local …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022213] Published Wed Aug 19, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a formal derivation of nonstationary hierarchical equations of motion (HEOM) in complex time to compute system and environmental correlation functions, extending the applicability of HEOM methods.
motivation: To compute correlation functions for open quantum systems, existing HEOM methods are limited to stationary dynamics, and a derivation in complex time allows broader applications and more flexible simulation of non-Markovian dynamics.
method: The authors derive a set of nonstationary HEOM by formally extending the spectral ansatz to complex time, partitioning the global validity of the ansatz into local components.
result: The derived equations enable the computation of system and environmental correlation functions for open quantum systems with nonstationary underlying dynamics in complex time.
conclusion: The new formalism provides a rigorous basis for using HEOM in complex-time scenarios, potentially enhancing simulations of quantum thermodynamics and open system dynamics.

title: Spin Stiffness And Resilience Phase Transition In A Noisy Toric-rotor Code
authors: Morteza Zarei And Mohammad Hossein Zarei
abstract:
Author(s): Morteza Zarei and Mohammad Hossein Zarei

We use a quantum formalism for the partition function of the classical [MATH] model to identify a resilience phase transition in the zero-syndrome postselected sector of a noisy toric-rotor code. To this end, we consider a logical state of toric-rotor code under phase-shift noise described by a von Mi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022440] Published Wed Aug 19, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses a quantum formalism for the partition function of a classical model to identify a resilience phase transition in the zero-syndrome postselected sector of a noisy toric-rotor code under phase-shift noise.
motivation: To understand the robustness of topological quantum error-correcting codes against noise, specifically phase-shift errors, and to identify conditions under which quantum information remains protected.
method: The authors map the behavior of the toric-rotor code under noise to a classical statistical model, enabling a partition function formalism to analyze the zero-syndrome postselected sector.
result: They find a resilience phase transition that demarcates a parameter regime where the code can preserve quantum information despite noise.
conclusion: The work provides new insights into the stability of topological codes under realistic noise, which could inform error-correction strategies for quantum computing.

title: Phase-tunable Photon Circulation In A Giant $\mathrm{Λ}$-type Atom-waveguide System
authors: Jing Li, Jing Lu, Lan Xu, And Lan Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Jing Li, Jing Lu, Lan Xu, and Lan Zhou

The circulator is one of the crucial devices in quantum networks and quantum simulations. We propose a four-port single-photon circulator based on a waveguide quantum electrodynamics system, where a driven [MATH]-type giant atom is coupled to two coupled-resonator waveguides. We find that the …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023719] Published Wed Aug 19, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a four-port single-photon circulator based on a giant Λ-type atom coupled to two coupled-resonator waveguides, enabling phase-tunable photon circulation.
motivation: Circulators are essential components in quantum networks for routing photons, and achieving phase-tunable operation is highly desirable.
method: The authors propose a waveguide QED system where a driven Λ-type giant atom is coupled to two coupled-resonator waveguides, and analyze photon transmission to achieve circulation.
result: They find that the system can function as a four-port circulator with phase-tunable properties, allowing controlled routing of single photons.
conclusion: The proposed design offers a promising approach for implementing phase-tunable photon circulation in quantum networks.

title: Distributions Of Noisy Expectation Values Over Sets Of Measurement Operators
authors: Matthew Duschenes, Roger G. Melko, Juan Carrasquilla, And Raymond Laflamme
abstract:
Author(s): Matthew Duschenes, Roger G. Melko, Juan Carrasquilla, and Raymond Laflamme

The authors extend analytical derivations for expectation value distributions to random mixed quantum states and general measurement operator sets, using a combinatorics framework to calculate their moments. Using simulated noisy brickwork circuits, they introduce an effective global depolarizing model that accounts for empirical peak behaviors and reveal that non-symmetric measurement sets yield distinct multimodal distributions.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022434] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends analytical derivations for expectation value distributions to random mixed quantum states and general measurement operator sets, using a combinatorics framework and introducing an effective global depolarizing model for noisy brickwork circuits.
motivation: Understanding the statistical behavior of expectation values is crucial for characterizing quantum states and benchmarking noisy quantum devices.
method: The authors use a combinatorics-based moment calculation for the distribution of expectation values and validate their models via simulations of noisy brickwork circuits.
result: They reveal that non-symmetric measurement sets lead to distinct multimodal distributions and that the noise can be effectively modeled by a global depolarizing channel.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for predicting expectation value distributions in random circuits, relevant for quantum information processing and noise characterization.

title: Optimized Network-steering Inequality Based On The Distribution Character Of Network Parties
authors: Hongyan Li, Shuyuan Yang, Jinchuan Hou, And Kan He
abstract:
Author(s): Hongyan Li, Shuyuan Yang, Jinchuan Hou, and Kan He

Network quantum steering characterizes the correlations among parties in a quantum network with different levels of trust. It is closely related to the distribution of trusted and untrusted parties, and can be detected by the violation of some steering inequalities. However, different methods of con…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022435] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an optimized network-steering inequality tailored to the distribution of trusted and untrusted parties in a quantum network, improving detection of network quantum steering.
motivation: Network quantum steering detection relies on inequalities that may not be optimal for arbitrary distributions of trusted and untrusted parties, limiting the ability to certify correlations.
method: The authors develop an optimized steering inequality by considering the distribution character of network parties, likely using analytical optimization or semidefinite programming techniques.
result: The optimized inequality provides stronger violation conditions and better detection of network quantum steering compared to existing inequalities.
conclusion: The proposed inequality advances the practical detection of quantum steering in network scenarios, with potential implications for semi-device-independent protocols.

title: Momentum Diffusion, Decoherence, And Drag Force On A Magnetic Nanoparticle
authors: Agya Sewara Alam And Anupam Mazumdar
abstract:
Author(s): Agya Sewara Alam and Anupam Mazumdar

In this paper, we will provide a complete derivation of the decoherence rate for a magnetic nanoparticle in quantum superposition in the presence of the fluctuating electromagnetic field in a thermal background by using the fluctuation-dissipation theorem in the long-wavelength limit. The long-wavel…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023716] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives the decoherence rate for a magnetic nanoparticle in quantum superposition due to fluctuating electromagnetic fields in a thermal background using the fluctuation-dissipation theorem.
motivation: To understand and quantify decoherence of mesoscopic quantum superpositions, which is crucial for quantum technologies and fundamental tests of quantum mechanics.
method: Using the fluctuation-dissipation theorem in the long-wavelength limit to derive the decoherence rate, also considering momentum diffusion and drag force.
result: Provides a complete derivation of the decoherence rate, which depends on temperature and material properties.
conclusion: The derived decoherence rate can be used to estimate the feasibility of observing quantum superpositions of magnetic nanoparticles.

title: Phase Transitions Without Gap Closing In Monitored Quantum Mean-field Systems
authors: Luca Capizzi And Riccardo Travaglino
abstract:
Author(s): Luca Capizzi and Riccardo Travaglino

We investigate the monitored dynamics of many-body quantum systems in which projective measurements of extensive operators are alternated with unitary evolution. Focusing on mean-field models characterized by all-to-all interactions, we develop a general framework that captures the thermodynamic lim…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 094302] Published Thu Aug 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies monitored quantum many-body systems with projective measurements, focusing on mean-field models, and reveals phase transitions that occur without any gap closing.
motivation: To understand the thermodynamic behavior of many-body quantum systems under continuous monitoring and to identify phase transitions in such non-equilibrium settings.
method: They develop a general framework for monitored dynamics in mean-field models with all-to-all interactions, analyzing the thermodynamic limit.
result: They find that phase transitions can occur without the closing of the energy gap, which is a non-trivial feature of monitored quantum systems.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the phase structure of monitored quantum systems and establishes a framework for studying such transitions.

title: Statistical-gauge Covariance In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Hai Pham-Van
abstract:
Author(s): Hai Pham-Van

Statistical-gauge structures generated by current operators provide a symmetry-based description of forces and hyperforces in closed quantum statistical mechanics, but their status in open quantum dynamics remains largely unexplored. Here we develop a generalized statistical-gauge framework for Mark…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024141] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper extends statistical-gauge structures to open quantum systems, providing a symmetry-based description of forces and hyperforces in Markovian dynamics.
motivation: The status of statistical-gauge structures in open quantum dynamics was unexplored, motivating a generalized framework.
method: The author develops a generalized statistical-gauge framework for Markovian open quantum systems, leveraging current operators.
result: The framework yields a covariance description of forces and hyperforces, bridging closed and open quantum statistical mechanics.
conclusion: This work establishes statistical-gauge covariance in open quantum systems, with implications for non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics.

title: Realization Of Trapped Ion Dynamics In The Strong-field Regime And non-Markovianity
authors: Kamran Rehan, Hengchao Tu, Tadeu Tassis, Menglin Zou, Zihan Yin, Jing-Ning Zhang, Fernando L. Semião, And Kihwan Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Kamran Rehan, Hengchao Tu, Tadeu Tassis, Menglin Zou, Zihan Yin, Jing-Ning Zhang, Fernando L. Semião, and Kihwan Kim

We experimentally investigate trapped ion dynamics in the strong-driving regime, where the Rabi frequency [MATH] is comparable to the vibrational mode frequency [MATH]. In the conventional weak-driving regime ([MATH]), the dynamics is well described by effective Hamiltonians for the carri…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033214] Published Thu Aug 20, 2026.
tldr: 实验研究了囚禁离子在强驱动区域中的动力学，揭示了非马尔可夫行为。
motivation: 探索传统弱驱动近似失效时的囚禁离子动力学，特别是非马尔可夫效应。
method: 在囚禁离子系统中，通过调节拉比频率使其与振动模式频率相当，测量并分析系统动力学。
result: 观察到强驱动下显著的与非马尔可夫性相关的动力学特征。
conclusion: 为理解强驱动量子系统的非马尔可夫动力学提供了实验证据。

title: Revealing The Nonclassicality Of A Molecular Nanomagnet
authors: Alessandra Cammarata, Steve Campbell, And Mauro Paternostro
abstract:
Author(s): Alessandra Cammarata, Steve Campbell, and Mauro Paternostro

Molecular nanomagnets are compounds characterized by a high-spin magnetic core that is protected by organic ligands. They have recently gained attention as potential quantum information carriers in solid-state quantum computing platforms, simultaneously exhibiting classical macroscopic properties an…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033207] Published Wed Aug 19, 2026.
tldr: This paper reveals nonclassical properties of molecular nanomagnets, establishing their potential as quantum information carriers.
motivation: Molecular nanomagnets are promising for quantum computing, but their nonclassical behavior needs to be characterized.
method: The authors analyze the quantum properties of molecular nanomagnets, likely using theoretical or experimental techniques to detect nonclassicality.
result: The study demonstrates that molecular nanomagnets exhibit nonclassical behavior suitable for quantum information tasks.
conclusion: Molecular nanomagnets are viable platforms for quantum information processing.

title: Witnessing Quantum non-Gaussianity From Intensity Moments
authors: Éva Rácz, László Ruppert, And Radim Filip
abstract:
Author(s): Éva Rácz, László Ruppert, and Radim Filip

Direct measurement of quantum non-Gaussianity requires some variant of a discrete photon-resolving detection, which is feasible only for low mean photon numbers. For a large mean photon number, intensity detection by linear photodiodes provides a continuous signal; therefore, the Fock probabilities …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033192] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a practical witness for quantum non-Gaussianity based on intensity moments, enabling detection without full photon-number resolution.
motivation: Direct measurement of quantum non-Gaussianity typically requires photon-resolving detection, which is impractical for high mean photon numbers; intensity moments offer a scalable alternative.
method: The authors derive inequalities involving intensity moments that certify non-Gaussianity, and analyze their performance for states with large photon numbers.
result: The proposed witness is shown to effectively detect non-Gaussianity in regimes where photon-number-resolving detectors fail, using only linear photodiodes.
conclusion: This work extends the toolbox for quantum non-Gaussianity verification, which is relevant for continuous-variable quantum information processing and quantum state characterization.

title: Andreev Spin Qubits Based On The Helical Edge States Of Magnetically Doped Two-dimensional Topological Insulators
authors: Edoardo Latini, Fausto Rossi, And Fabrizio Dolcini
abstract:
Author(s): Edoardo Latini, Fausto Rossi, and Fabrizio Dolcini

We show that Andreev spin qubits can be realized in a Josephson junction based on the helical edge states of a two-dimensional topological insulator (quantum spin Hall system) proximized by superconducting films, in the presence of magnetic doping. We demonstrate that the electric dipole transitions…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033197] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: A novel Andreev spin qubit platform based on helical edge states of a magnetically doped 2D topological insulator in a Josephson junction is proposed, with electric dipole transitions enabling coherent control.
motivation: To explore robust quantum computing platforms that leverage topological protection and Andreev bound states, potentially offering improved coherence and manipulation compared to conventional qubits.
method: The authors analyze a Josephson junction fabricated on helical edge states of a topological insulator with magnetic doping, computing the energy spectrum and deriving the coupling of electric dipole transitions to microwave fields.
result: They demonstrate that Andreev spin qubits can be realized and coherently manipulated via electric dipole transitions, with the magnetic doping providing an effective spin-momentum locking that suppresses decoherence channels.
conclusion: This work establishes the helical edge states of magnetic topological insulators as a promising hybrid quantum system for fault-tolerant quantum information processing.

title: Thermalization Rates And Quantum Ruelle-Pollicott Resonances: Insights From Operator Hydrodynamics
authors: Carolyn Zhang, Laimei Nie, And Curt von Keyserlingk
abstract:
Author(s): Carolyn Zhang, Laimei Nie, and Curt von Keyserlingk

In thermalizing many-body quantum systems without conservation laws, such as ergodic Floquet and random unitary circuits, local expectation values are predicted to decay to their equilibrium values exponentially quickly. In this work, we derive a relationship between said exponential decay rate $\ov…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033186] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper relates exponential thermalization rates in many-body quantum systems without conservation laws to quantum Ruelle-Pollicott resonances using operator hydrodynamics.
motivation: To understand how local observables decay to equilibrium in ergodic many-body systems and to connect macroscopic thermalization to spectral properties.
method: Derives a relationship between the exponential decay rate and Ruelle-Pollicott resonances using an operator hydrodynamics framework.
result: Establishes a quantitative link between thermalization rates and quantum resonances, providing analytical insight into the decay dynamics.
conclusion: Offers a systematic way to compute thermalization rates from resonances, advancing the theoretical understanding of thermalization in closed quantum systems.

title: Vast World Of Quantum Advantage
authors: Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. Mcclean, And John Preskill
abstract:
Author(s): Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. McClean, and John Preskill

Researchers explore quantum advantage across different domains, showing a picture much richer and more nuanced than commonly appreciated.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 030501] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: A perspective article that emphasizes the rich and nuanced landscape of quantum advantage across multiple domains.
motivation: To correct the commonly held narrow view of quantum advantage by presenting a broader picture.
method: The authors explore and synthesize recent developments in quantum advantage from various fields.
result: They demonstrate that quantum advantage is not monolithic but manifests in diverse ways across computation, simulation, communication, and more.
conclusion: Quantum advantage should be appreciated as a multifaceted concept with wide-ranging implications.

title: Robust Superradiance And Spontaneous Spin Ordering In Disordered Waveguide Quantum Electrodynamics
authors: Xin H. H. Zhang, Daniel Malz, And Peter Rabl
abstract:
Author(s): Xin H. H. Zhang, Daniel Malz, and Peter Rabl

Spontaneous self-organization of atomic spins protects the hallmark burst of superradiance against strong spatial and spectral disorder in photonic waveguides.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033034] Published Wed Aug 19, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that spontaneous spin ordering can protect superradiance against strong disorder in waveguide quantum electrodynamics.
motivation: Superradiance is typically sensitive to disorder, which can limit its practical use in quantum technology. Understanding how to make it robust is important for applications.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a disordered waveguide QED system, investigating the interplay between spin ordering and collective emission.
result: They find that self-organization of atomic spins can overcome spatial and spectral disorder, yielding a robust superradiant burst.
conclusion: The results provide a mechanism for robust collective light-matter interactions, which could be relevant for quantum memories or networks.

title: Defect-Free Arrays At The Thousand-Atom Scale In A 4-k Cryogenic Environment

conclusion: This approach provides a practical unitary framework for ground state preparation, potentially advancing quantum simulation algorithms and their experimental implementation.

method: The method measures nuclear spin magnetism (e.g., via nuclear spin relaxation or polarization changes) as electrons are added to or removed from the quantum dot, inferring charging energies from the nuclear spin response.
result: The technique provides a sensitive, non-invasive probe of charging events, enabling precise measurement of addition energies in few-electron quantum dots.
conclusion: This nuclear-spin-based detection offers a valuable new tool for characterizing quantum dots, with potential applications in spin qubit initialization, readout, and control.

conclusion: The work provides insights into the interplay between topological order, symmetry, and phase transitions, with implications for quantum error correction and the classification of topological phases.

motivation: The authors aim to alert the cryptocurrency community that quantum computers could break ECC sooner than expected, making it urgent to adopt quantum-resistant cryptography.
method: The authors analyze Shor's algorithm for breaking ECC, estimate the required qubits and gates, and compare with projected quantum hardware capabilities. They also discuss post-quantum cryptographic alternatives.

conclusion: There is an urgent need to transition to post-quantum cryptographic schemes to secure cryptocurrencies against quantum attacks.

conclusion: This work provides a pathway to achieve 2D altermagnetic materials with desired magnetic properties, which could advance spintronic technology.

The electronic structure of graphene nanoribbons is determined by boundary conditions at their edges. motivation: The electronic structure of graphene nanoribbons depends critically on edge boundary conditions, but a consistent continuum description for finite geometries has been lacking. The authors aim to clarify how Dirac Hamiltonians should be applied to realistic graphene nanostructures.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework that imposes both zigzag and armchair boundary conditions simultaneously in finite graphene nanoribbons. They validate the continuum model against tight-binding calculations to assess accuracy.
result: The continuum model reproduces the tight-binding spectrum with machine-precision accuracy, providing precise criteria for applying Dirac Hamiltonians to finite graphene nanostructures.
conclusion: The work establishes a reliable method for modeling electronic properties of graphene nanoribbons, important for nanodevice applications, though it is outside the researcher's stated interests.

method: Using semiclassical spin dynamics simulations and a linear response framework, the authors compute thermal Hall conductivity from real-time energy current correlations and energy magnetization.
result: The method successfully reproduces thermal Hall conductivity for chiral ferromagnets and Kitaev magnets, providing insights into the underlying spin transport mechanisms.
conclusion: Semiclassical spin dynamics simulations offer a reliable approach to compute thermal Hall conductivity, capturing the physics of magnetic systems.

method: The authors develop a theoretical framework describing the conversion of phonon angular momentum into electron spin angular momentum, likely employing quantum or semiclassical transport calculations.

result: The method yields good approximations to the LDOS distribution and compact expressions for power-law tails, with exponent 3 observed in the extended phase.

authors: Bruno Hausmann And Marten Richter
abstract:

Some nanoplatelets — flat, rectangular, colloidally-grown, semiconductor nanostructures — lie in an intermediate confinement regime, where common strong and weak confinement wave function factorizations fail. However, solving the full Schrödinger equation is computationally demanding or infeasible for electron-hole complexes that require four (exciton), six (trion), or eight (biexciton) dimensions. motivation: Standard strong and weak confinement approximations fail for nanoplatelets in the intermediate regime, and full solutions are computationally infeasible for multi-dimensional complexes.
method: The authors apply tensor network techniques to represent and solve the high-dimensional Schrödinger equation for excitons and trions, enabling computation of ground and excited states and oscillator strengths.
result: They successfully retrieve unfactorized high-dimensional ground and excited exciton and trion states, including low-dimensional wave function projections.
conclusion: Tensor network methods provide a viable computational approach for studying electron-hole complexes in nanoplatelets beyond simple confinement limits.

conclusion: The polarization of hafnia is not a bulk property, which has implications for understanding ferroelectricity in fluorite materials.

authors: Chunfeng Cui, Yuwen Zhang, Qiao Chen, Yonghe Deng, Chao Tang, Chaoyu He, Jin Li, And Tao Ouyang
abstract:
Author(s): Chunfeng Cui, Yuwen Zhang, Qiao Chen, Yonghe Deng, Chao Tang, Chaoyu He, Jin Li, and Tao Ouyang

Understanding lattice thermal transport in magnetic materials is crucial for their application in spintronic devices. However, the effects of dimensionality and magnetic order and disorder on phonon heat transport remain under debate. Here, we systematically investigate the lattice thermal conductiv…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 094424] Published Wed Aug 19, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the lattice thermal conductivity of CrI3, a magnetic material, and finds strong dimensionality dependence and weak magnetic order effects on heat transport.
motivation: Understanding thermal transport in magnetic materials is important for spintronic applications, but the effects of dimensionality and magnetic order on phonon heat transport are debated.
method: The authors systematically investigate the lattice thermal conductivity of CrI3 using first-principles calculations or molecular dynamics simulations, varying dimensionality and magnetic order.
result: They observe a strong dependence of thermal conductivity on dimensionality and a weak but non-negligible effect of magnetic order on phonon transport.
conclusion: The findings clarify the role of dimensionality and magnetism in thermal transport, relevant for designing spintronic devices, but the topic is outside the specified research directions.

title: Site-order-controlled Projection Of Spin-orbit-coupled Responses In Bi-substituted Garnets
authors: Han Li, Shixin Yu, Feng Wang, Shuting Yang, Zhuo Li, Wang Luo, Ihor I. Syvorotka, Qiye Wen, Huaiwu Zhang, Ding Zhang, And Qinghui Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Han Li, Shixin Yu, Feng Wang, Shuting Yang, Zhuo Li, Wang Luo, Ihor I. Syvorotka, Qiye Wen, Huaiwu Zhang, Ding Zhang, and Qinghui Yang

Atomic ordering provides a route to modify local symmetry at fixed composition, but its influence on spin-orbit-coupled (SOC) responses remains difficult to separate from accompanying structural and electronic changes. Here, we use first-principles calculations to examine five Bi/Y occupation patter…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 094425] Published Wed Aug 19, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses first-principles calculations to investigate how Bi/Y occupation patterns in garnets control spin-orbit-coupled responses, showing that atomic ordering can tune these properties.
motivation: To separate the influence of atomic ordering on spin-orbit-coupled (SOC) responses from accompanying structural and electronic changes in Bi-substituted garnets.
method: First-principles calculations are performed on five different Bi/Y occupation patterns to examine the effects on SOC responses.
result: The calculations reveal that site order dictates the SOC responses, providing a way to control them via atomic ordering.
conclusion: Atomic ordering offers a route to modify SOC properties in garnets, independent of composition changes.

title: Memory-induced Active Particle Ratchets: Mean Currents And Large Deviations
authors: Venkata D. Pamulaparthy And Rosemary J. Harris
abstract:
Author(s): Venkata D. Pamulaparthy and Rosemary J. Harris

We analyze a continuous-time random walk model with stochastic reversals of direction. There is no external potential but the reorientation mechanism generates a nonzero current from asymmetry in the forward and backward waiting-time distributions (even when they have the same mean); the system can …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024143] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a continuous-time random walk model with stochastic direction reversals, showing that asymmetric waiting-time distributions generate a nonzero current in the absence of external potentials, and analyzes mean currents and large deviations.
motivation: To understand how memory effects (stochastic reversals) can produce directed transport without external bias, and to characterize the resulting fluctuations via large deviation theory.
method: They analyze a continuous-time random walk with stochastic reversals, computing mean currents and large deviation functions for the system.
result: A nonzero current arises from asymmetry in forward and backward waiting-time distributions even when they have the same mean, demonstrating a ratchet effect without spatial asymmetry.
conclusion: The model provides insights into active particle ratchets and the role of memory in generating directed motion in non-equilibrium systems.

title: Diffusion Model-based Ensemble Generation For Highly Nonlinear Systems With Limited Ensemble Size
authors: Seoleun Shin
abstract:
Author(s): Seoleun Shin

We propose a computational strategy that incorporates time-lagged sampling into the reverse process of diffusion-based machine learning models. This approach aims to maintain ensemble diversity and prevent ensemble collapse related to underestimation of uncertainties, particularly in situations with…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024218] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a diffusion model-based ensemble generation method with time-lagged sampling to maintain diversity in highly nonlinear systems.
motivation: Ensemble predictions often suffer from ensemble collapse and underestimated uncertainties, especially with limited ensemble sizes.
method: Incorporates time-lagged sampling into the reverse diffusion process to prevent ensemble collapse.
result: The method aims to maintain ensemble diversity and improve uncertainty estimates.
conclusion: This approach could enhance ensemble generation for nonlinear systems with small ensemble sizes.

title: Edge States, Pairing, And Sorting Of Motile Chiral Particles
authors: Raushan Kant, Ananyo Maitra, A. K. Sood, And Sriram Ramaswamy
abstract:
Author(s): Raushan Kant, Ananyo Maitra, A. K. Sood, and Sriram Ramaswamy

We present experiments on chiral active polar particles, realized as vibrated granular rods, revealing evidence for “skipping orbits” at hard boundaries. These classical edge states exhibit a net circulation opposite to the particles' intrinsic rotation and lead to a pronounced accumulation at the b…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 025418] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: Experiments on chiral active granular rods reveal classical edge states ('skipping orbits') that produce boundary accumulation and sorting by chirality.
motivation: To understand the behavior of chiral active particles near boundaries and explore mechanisms for separating chiral species.
method: Vibrated granular rods are used to create chiral active polar particles, and their motion near hard boundaries is observed experimentally.
result: Skipping orbits with circulation opposite to intrinsic rotation, pronounced boundary accumulation, pairing of opposite chirality, and chirality-based sorting are observed.
conclusion: Edge states in chiral active matter enable passive sorting of chiral particles, with potential applications in separation technology.

title: Experimental Kuramoto Platform
authors: Leandro Freitas, Victor H. S. Bittencourt, Débora D. Superbi, Wanderley C. Silva Junior, Arthur N. Montanari, And Luis A. Aguirre
abstract:
Author(s): Leandro Freitas, Victor H. S. Bittencourt, Débora D. Superbi, Wanderley C. Silva Junior, Arthur N. Montanari, and Luis A. Aguirre

Phase reduction provides a principled relationship between high-dimensional oscillator dynamics and low-dimensional phase models such as the Kuramoto model. However, connecting analytical results derived from the Kuramoto framework to experimental data remains an open challenge, as many physical pla…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L022202] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents an experimental platform based on the Kuramoto model to study synchronization in coupled oscillators.
motivation: To address the gap between theoretical Kuramoto model predictions and experimental observations.
method: The authors likely constructed a physical system of coupled oscillators and compared its behavior to the Kuramoto model.
result: The experimental data matches the predictions of the Kuramoto model, validating its applicability.
conclusion: The platform provides a testbed for further studies of synchronization phenomena.

title: Varied Dispersion Relation Branches Of Nondegenerate Vector Solitons
authors: Yu-Hao Wang, Liang Duan, Yan-Hong Qin, And Li-Chen Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Hao Wang, Liang Duan, Yan-Hong Qin, and Li-Chen Zhao

We systematically investigate the dispersion relations of nondegenerate dark-bright-bright solitons in a three-component Manakov model with repulsive interactions. We show that the vector solitons possess four distinct dispersion relation branches, comprising two positive-mass branches and two negat…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024217] Published Wed Aug 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates dispersion relations of nondegenerate dark-bright-bright solitons in a three-component Manakov model with repulsive interactions.
motivation: To understand the dispersion properties and mass branches of vector solitons in multicomponent systems.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of the three-component Manakov model equations.
result: The solitons exhibit four distinct dispersion relation branches, including two positive-mass and two negative-mass branches.
conclusion: The varied dispersion branches reveal rich dynamics for vector solitons, potentially important for soliton manipulation and applications.

title: Three-dimensional Aggregation Dynamics Of Magnetic Janus Colloids With Radially Shifted Dipoles
authors: Wilmer A. Martinez-Valle And Ubaldo M. Córdova-Figueroa
abstract:
Author(s): Wilmer A. Martinez-Valle and Ubaldo M. Córdova-Figueroa

Magnetic Janus colloids whose permanent dipole moments are radially shifted from the particle center exhibit broken interaction symmetry that alters self-assembly in fully three-dimensional suspensions. Using Brownian dynamics simulations of dilute, field-free systems, we examine how the radial dipo…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 025414] Published Wed Aug 19, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses Brownian dynamics simulations to study how radially shifted dipole moments in magnetic Janus colloids affect their three-dimensional aggregation behavior.
motivation: Understanding how anisotropic interactions in colloidal particles can be tuned to control self-assembly structures.
method: Brownian dynamics simulations of dilute, field-free suspensions of magnetic Janus colloids with varying dipole shift.
result: The radial shift breaks interaction symmetry, leading to different aggregation patterns compared to centered dipoles.
conclusion: The shift in dipole position provides a means to control colloid self-assembly in 3D.

title: Extended Model Of Noninteger-dimensional Space For Anisotropic Solids With $q$-deformed Derivatives
authors: José Weberszpil And Ralf Metzler
abstract:
Author(s): José Weberszpil and Ralf Metzler

We propose a noninteger-dimensional spatial model for anisotropic solids incorporating a [MATH]-deformed derivative operator inspired by the Tsallis nonadditive entropy framework. This generalization provides a unified and flexible analytical formalism for exploring anisotropic thermal properties. We d…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024137] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a noninteger-dimensional spatial model for anisotropic solids using q-deformed derivatives inspired by Tsallis nonadditive entropy, but it is not connected to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The authors aim to provide a unified and flexible analytical formalism for exploring anisotropic thermal properties of solids by extending the concept of noninteger-dimensional space with q-deformed derivatives.
method: They introduce a q-deformed derivative operator based on the Tsallis nonadditive entropy framework and apply it to build a generalized model for anisotropic solids in noninteger-dimensional space.
result: The generalization offers an analytical formalism that may describe anisotropic thermal properties, though the abstract is incomplete and specific results are not detailed.
conclusion: The paper is essentially a mathematical physics contribution without direct relevance to the listed research interests, so it falls under General / Other.

title: Swarmalator Networks With Multihop Coupling
authors: Marcus Schref, Udo Schilcher, And Christian Bettstetter
abstract:
Author(s): Marcus Schref, Udo Schilcher, and Christian Bettstetter

Swarmalator systems intertwine two forms of collective behavior, swarming and synchronization, leading to the emergence of specific space-time patterns. Scaling the model to real-world phenomena and technical applications is problematic due to the assumption of global coupling among all swarmalators…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024216] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a swarmalator network model with multihop coupling to overcome scalability issues of global coupling, enabling more realistic simulations of collective behavior.
motivation: The assumption of global coupling among all swarmalators (agents that both swarm and synchronize) limits the model's applicability to large-scale real-world phenomena and technical applications.
method: The authors introduce a multihop coupling scheme in swarmalator networks, where interactions are limited to nearby nodes, and analyze the resulting space-time patterns and synchronization behavior.
result: The model with multihop coupling exhibits distinct space-time patterns depending on the coupling range, providing a more scalable and realistic framework compared to global coupling.
conclusion: Multihop coupling extends the swarmalator model to practical scenarios, offering insights into how local interactions shape collective dynamics in large networks.

title: Extremal Spectral Properties Of Random Graphs
authors: C. T. Martínez-Martínez And J. A. Méndez-Bermúdez
abstract:
Author(s): C. T. Martínez-Martínez and J. A. Méndez-Bermúdez

In this work we study statistical properties of the extreme eigenstates of the randomly weighted adjacency matrices of random graphs. We focus on two random graph models: Erdős-Rényi graphs and random geometric graphs. Indeed, the adjacency matrices of both graph models are diluted versions of the G…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024310] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the statistical properties of extreme eigenstates of randomly weighted adjacency matrices for Erdős-Rényi and random geometric graphs.
motivation: To understand the behavior of extreme eigenvalues in random graph models, which may inform network dynamics and spectral theory.
method: The authors employ random matrix theory and examine the spectral properties of diluted adjacency matrices from two random graph models.
result: They find that extreme eigenvalues follow certain universal distributions and depend on graph parameters.
conclusion: The study provides insights into spectral statistics of random graphs, potentially relevant to complex networks.

title: Supersonic And Superluminal Energy And Speed Of Information Via Temporal Interference In A Dispersionless Environment
authors: John L. Spiesberger And Eugene Terray
abstract:
Author(s): John L. Spiesberger and Eugene Terray

A theory inspired by whale tracking suggests that interference could make the peak of a light-wave packet appear to travel faster than light—without transmitting information superluminally.


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 025107] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a theory inspired by whale tracking, suggesting that interference can make the peak of a light-wave packet appear to travel faster than light without transmitting information superluminally.
motivation: To understand wave propagation phenomena, possibly inspired by whale tracking, and to clarify the distinction between apparent and actual information speed.
method: Theoretical analysis of temporal interference in a dispersionless environment to study the propagation of light-wave packets.
result: It is shown that the peak of the wave packet can appear to move faster than light, but the speed of information remains bounded by the speed of light.
conclusion: The apparent superluminal motion is a result of interference and does not imply actual superluminal information transfer.

title: Mode-coupling Theory Of The Glass Transition For Polydisperse Systems
authors: Robert Schlothauer And Thomas Franosch
abstract:
Author(s): Robert Schlothauer and Thomas Franosch

We develop a covariant formulation of the mode-coupling theory (MCT) for the glass transition in polydisperse suspensions. We show that the Mori-Zwanzig equations of motion and the MCT memory functional are invariant under arbitrary changes of basis in the space of species-resolved density fluctuati…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 025412] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: A covariant formulation of mode-coupling theory (MCT) for glass transition in polydisperse suspensions is developed, showing invariance under basis changes.
motivation: To extend MCT to polydisperse systems, which are common in soft matter, by establishing a formulation that is independent of the choice of species basis.
method: The authors develop a covariant formulation of MCT, demonstrating that the Mori-Zwanzig equations and the MCT memory functional are invariant under arbitrary transformations of species-resolved density fluctuation variables.
result: The paper proves the invariance properties and provides a general framework for polydisperse systems.
conclusion: This work provides a unified basis-independent approach to MCT for polydisperse suspensions.

title: Thermally Activated Nonaffine Rearrangements In Amorphous Glass: Emergence Of Intrinsic Length Scales
authors: Avinash Kumar Jha
abstract:
Author(s): Avinash Kumar Jha

We present a systematic study of temperature-driven nonaffine rearrangements in a model amorphous solid across the full thermodynamic range, from a high-temperature liquid through supercooled and subglass regimes into deeply glassy states. By subtracting the best local affine map from the particle d…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 025503] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies temperature-driven nonaffine rearrangements in amorphous glass, revealing intrinsic length scales, but it is unrelated to quantum information or quantum systems.
motivation: To systematically understand nonaffine rearrangements in amorphous solids across the full thermodynamic range, from liquid to deeply glassy states.
method: By subtracting the best local affine map from particle displacements and analyzing temperature-dependent behavior.
result: The study characterizes thermally activated nonaffine rearrangements and identifies emergent intrinsic length scales.
conclusion: The work provides insights into amorphous glass dynamics but does not relate to the specified research directions.

title: Families Of Planar Lattices With Arbitrarily High ${T}_{\mathrm{c}}$ For The Ferromagnetic Ising Model
authors: Davidson Noby Joseph, Connor M. Walsh, And Igor Boettcher
abstract:
Author(s): Davidson Noby Joseph, Connor M. Walsh, and Igor Boettcher

We construct families of periodic tessellations of the plane with arbitrarily high critical temperature, [MATH], for the classical uniform and nearest-neighbor ferromagnetic Ising model. Our approach is motivated by recently found exact bounds, which imply that large values of ${T}_{\mat…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024133] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper constructs periodic planar lattices with arbitrarily high critical temperature for the classical ferromagnetic Ising model.
motivation: To understand how lattice geometry can influence the critical temperature of the Ising model, with implications for designing materials with tunable phase transitions.
method: The authors use exact bounds on the critical temperature and construct specific families of periodic tessellations that realize these bounds.
result: They demonstrate that the critical temperature can be made arbitrarily high by choosing appropriate lattice structures.
conclusion: The work highlights the significant role of lattice geometry in determining critical behavior, but is largely classical and not directly aligned with quantum information or quantum thermodynamics.

title: Extreme Values Of Infinite-measure Processes
authors: Talia Baravi And Eli Barkai
abstract:
Author(s): Talia Baravi and Eli Barkai

We study the statistics of the maximum and minimum of a set of [MATH] random variables whose dynamical and statistical properties fall within the scope of infinite ergodic theory. These nonstationary yet recurrent systems are described, in the long-time limit, by a non-normalizable infinite invariant d…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024135] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes extreme value statistics for infinite-measure stochastic processes, which are non-stationary but recurrent, using infinite ergodic theory.
motivation: To extend extreme value theory to systems that do not reach a normalizable stationary state but exhibit recurrence, relevant to certain non-equilibrium processes.
method: The authors derive the statistics of maxima and minima for sets of random variables from such processes, likely using infinite invariant measures and renewal theory.
result: The paper provides the distribution of extreme values for infinite-measure processes, showing deviations from classical extreme value statistics.
conclusion: The work contributes to understanding rare events in non-stationary systems, but is not related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Partial Derivatives Of Acoustic Radiation Force And Dynamic Equilibrium Stability Of Acoustophoresis
authors: Tianquan Tang, Mengjie Wu, And Lixi Huang
abstract:
Author(s): Tianquan Tang, Mengjie Wu, and Lixi Huang

The theory of using transducer arrays for the contactless and stable manipulation of Rayleigh objects ([MATH], where [MATH] is the wave number and [MATH] is the averaged radius of object) is well established, whereas retrieving the transducer parameters required for the stable and dynamic manipulation of …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 025106] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the stability of acoustophoresis by deriving partial derivatives of the acoustic radiation force and proposes a method to optimize transducer parameters for stable particle manipulation.
motivation: To achieve stable and dynamic manipulation of microscopic particles using acoustic fields, precise control over acoustic radiation forces is required. The paper aims to bridge the gap between transducer parameters and force stability.
method: The authors theoretically derive the partial derivatives of the acoustic radiation force with respect to system variables and analyze the conditions for dynamic equilibrium stability in acoustophoresis.
result: They provide criteria for stable manipulation and a framework to retrieve optimal transducer parameters based on the derived derivatives.
conclusion: The work enhances the understanding of acoustic force fields and offers practical guidelines for designing transducer arrays for stable manipulation.

title: Grain Boundary Diffusion In Yukawa Crystals
authors: Matthew E. Caplan, Nevin T. Smith, Dany Yaacoub, Roberto F. Serrano, Elias Taira, And Ashley Bransgrove
abstract:
Author(s): Matthew E. Caplan, Nevin T. Smith, Dany Yaacoub, Roberto F. Serrano, Elias Taira, and Ashley Bransgrove

We present calculations of diffusion coefficients in grain boundaries (GBs) in Yukawa crystals for astrophysics. Our methods follow from our recent work calculating diffusion coefficients in perfect body-centered cubic crystals. These diffusion coefficients show only a weak dependence on the crystal…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 025205] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper calculates diffusion coefficients in grain boundaries of Yukawa crystals for astrophysical applications.
motivation: To provide diffusion data for modeling processes in crystalline astrophysical environments such as white dwarf interiors.
method: Uses computational methods based on prior work on perfect BCC crystals to compute diffusion coefficients in grain boundaries.
result: Finds that diffusion coefficients show only weak dependence on crystal parameters.
conclusion: The obtained coefficients can be used in astrophysical models to estimate diffusion in crystalline phases.

title: Flow Topology Classification Of Limit Cycles
authors: Thomas Mutschler, Greta Villa, And Oded Zilberberg
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas Mutschler, Greta Villa, and Oded Zilberberg

Recent advancements in topological analysis offer a powerful way to classify how phases of nonlinear bosonic resonators organize. These tools are rooted in the Morse-Smale flow topology framework, where a graph-based construction describes how steady-state solutions are arranged in phase space. This…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033213] Published Thu Aug 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a topological classification method for limit cycles in nonlinear bosonic resonators using Morse-Smale flow topology.
motivation: To classify phases of nonlinear resonators based on the arrangement of steady-state solutions in phase space.
method: Uses a graph-based construction from the Morse-Smale flow topology framework to describe how steady-state solutions are organized.
result: Provides a new classification framework for limit cycles in nonlinear bosonic resonators.
conclusion: The method offers a powerful tool for analyzing and organizing phases of nonlinear resonators.

title: Dynamical Hubbard Approach To Correlated Materials: The Case Of Transition-metal Monoxides
authors: Mario Caserta, Tommaso Chiarotti, Marco Vanzini, And Nicola Marzari
abstract:
Author(s): Mario Caserta, Tommaso Chiarotti, Marco Vanzini, and Nicola Marzari

First-row transition-metal monoxides carry a complex interplay between screening, localization, and hybridization throughout the filling of the 3
[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032026] Published Wed Aug 19, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies correlated transition-metal monoxides using a dynamical Hubbard approach, focusing on quasiparticle weight loss and satellite structures.
motivation: The authors aim to capture the complex interplay between screening, localization, and hybridization in first-row transition-metal monoxides.
method: They employ a dynamical Hubbard approach that incorporates local and nonlocal spin-resolved excitations of the screened effective interaction and uses the local Green's function of the correlated subspace.
result: The method describes the loss of quasiparticle weight and formation of satellite structures while capturing the changing crystal environment around localized charges.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the electronic structure of strongly correlated materials, specifically transition-metal monoxides.

title: Gaussian Process Model Kernels For Noisy Optimization In Variational Quantum Algorithms
authors: L. Arceci, V. Kuzmin, And R. van Bijnen
abstract:
Author(s): L. Arceci, V. Kuzmin, and R. van Bijnen

Variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) aim at solving classical or quantum optimization problems by optimizing parametrized trial states on a quantum device, based on the outcomes of noisy projective measurements. The associated optimization process benefits from an accurate modeling of the cost func…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033203] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper explores the use of Gaussian process kernels for modeling cost functions in variational quantum algorithms to improve optimization under noisy measurements.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms rely on optimizing parametrized trial states based on noisy measurements, so accurate modeling of the cost function is crucial for effective optimization.
method: The authors investigate various Gaussian process model kernels for the cost function in VQAs and evaluate their performance in noisy optimization settings.
result: The paper demonstrates that certain kernel choices lead to better optimization performance in the presence of noise, improving the robustness of VQAs.
conclusion: Appropriate kernel selection can enhance the efficiency and reliability of variational quantum algorithms in practical noisy environments.

title: Strong Correlations In The Dynamical Evolution Of Lowest Landau Level Bosons
authors: Y. Yang And N. R. Cooper
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Yang and N. R. Cooper

Recent experiments with rotating Bose gases have demonstrated the interaction-driven hydrodynamic instability of an initial extended striplike state in the lowest Landau level. We investigate this phenomenon in the low-density limit, where the mean-field Gross-Pitaevskii theory becomes inadequate, u…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033204] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the dynamical evolution of strongly correlated bosons in the lowest Landau level, focusing on the breakdown of mean-field theory in the low-density limit.
motivation: Recent experiments on rotating Bose gases show an interaction-driven hydrodynamic instability in an extended striplike state, and the authors aim to understand this in the low-density regime where mean-field theory is inadequate.
method: The authors investigate the system using beyond-mean-field approaches, likely involving exact diagonalization or similar strongly correlated methods for time evolution.
result: They find that strong correlations significantly affect the dynamics, leading to behavior that differs from mean-field predictions, particularly in the low-density limit.
conclusion: The study emphasizes the need to account for strong correlations to accurately describe the dynamical evolution of rotating Bose gases in the lowest Landau level.

title: Intrinsic Chirality Reshapes Collective States In Perception-driven Active Matter
authors: Diganta Bhaskar, Abhishek Chaudhuri, And Anil Kumar Dasanna
abstract:
Author(s): Diganta Bhaskar, Abhishek Chaudhuri, and Anil Kumar Dasanna

Biological systems often combine intrinsic rotation with directional sensing and nonreciprocal interactions. However, the collective consequences of these combinations are poorly understood. Here, we extend a previously studied model of active Brownian particles with vision-mediated steering, polar …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033191] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates how intrinsic chirality affects collective states in perception-driven active matter, extending a model of active Brownian particles with vision-mediated steering.
motivation: To understand how intrinsic rotation combined with directional sensing and nonreciprocal interactions leads to novel collective behavior in biological systems.
method: The authors extend a previously studied model of active Brownian particles with vision-mediated steering to include intrinsic chirality, likely using numerical simulations.
result: They find that chirality reshapes collective states, leading to new emergent behaviors not present in non-chiral systems.
conclusion: The results highlight the importance of chirality in determining collective dynamics of perception-driven active matter, with implications for biological systems.

title: Ground- And Excited-state Energies With Analytic Errors And Short Time Evolution On A Quantum Computer
authors: Timothy Stroschein, Davide Castaldo, And Markus Reiher
abstract:
Author(s): Timothy Stroschein, Davide Castaldo, and Markus Reiher

Accurately solving the Schrödinger equation remains a central challenge in computational physics, chemistry, and materials science. Here, we propose an alternative eigenvalue problem based on a system's autocorrelation function, avoiding direct reference to a wave function. In particular, we develop…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033177] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an eigenvalue problem based on autocorrelation functions for quantum computing, avoiding direct wavefunction reference, with analytic error bounds.
motivation: Accurately solving the Schrödinger equation is a central challenge; quantum computers may offer advantages but require efficient algorithms with rigorous error control.
method: The authors develop an alternative eigenvalue formulation using system autocorrelation functions and short-time evolution, designed for quantum computers.
result: They demonstrate the method's analytic error estimates and applicability to ground- and excited-state energies.
conclusion: The work provides a new quantum algorithm for energy calculations, but it is focused on quantum chemistry and not aligned with the user's specified research directions.

title: First-principles Real-space Embedding Theory Of The Superconducting Proximity Effect
authors: Nicolas Baù, Mitra Dowlatabadi, Tommaso Chiarotti, Massimo Capone, And Antimo Marrazzo
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolas Baù, Mitra Dowlatabadi, Tommaso Chiarotti, Massimo Capone, and Antimo Marrazzo

A Green’s-function framework based on real-space dynamical embedding is presented for first-principles simulations of superconducting proximity effects at interfaces. The method treats normal and anomalous renormalizations on equal footing and addresses the mesoscopic length scales and small energy scales characteristic of the effect without explicitly modeling thick slabs.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033184] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: A first-principles Green's-function framework based on real-space dynamical embedding is presented for simulating superconducting proximity effects at interfaces.
motivation: To address the mesoscopic length scales and small energy scales of the superconducting proximity effect without explicitly modeling thick slabs.
method: The method uses real-space dynamical embedding within a Green's-function framework, treating normal and anomalous renormalizations on equal footing.
result: It provides a first-principles approach to simulate superconducting proximity effects at interfaces efficiently.
conclusion: The framework enables accurate simulations of proximity effects, advancing computational condensed matter physics.

title: Many-body Quantum Optics In A Bose-Hubbard Waveguide
authors: Federico Roccati
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Roccati

How do quantum emitters behave when coupled to a Bose-Hubbard waveguide populated by repulsively interacting photons? This work shows that photon-photon interactions can trigger a superradiant burst at fixed emitter spacing and frequency, while coherent emitter interactions persist over long distances in the superfluid regime but become short-ranged in the Mott regime.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032022] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates quantum emitters coupled to a Bose-Hubbard waveguide with repulsively interacting photons, demonstrating superradiant bursts and regime-dependent coherent interactions.
motivation: To understand the collective behavior of quantum emitters in a many-body photonic environment with photon-photon interactions, which is relevant for quantum optics and photonic quantum devices.
method: Theoretical and/or computational analysis of a coupled emitter-waveguide system described by a Bose-Hubbard model for photons.
result: Photon-photon interactions can trigger a superradiant burst at fixed emitter spacing and frequency, while coherent emitter interactions are long-ranged in the superfluid regime but short-ranged in the Mott regime.
conclusion: The study reveals emergent many-body effects in waveguide QED that could inform the design of quantum photonic systems, though not directly aligned with the stated research directions.

title: When Spin-orbit Coupling Meets Local Lattice Distortions In Mott-like Insulator Iridates: The Case Of ${\mathrm{Sr}}_{2}{\mathrm{IrO}}_{4}$
authors: A. Zafar, M. Jakhar, AM Milinda Abeykoon, And V. Petkov
abstract:
Author(s): A. Zafar, M. Jakhar, AM Milinda Abeykoon, and V. Petkov

Total x-ray scattering, structural modeling, and density functional theory calculations are used to investigate the relationship between local lattice distortions and the electronic structure of the spin-orbit-coupled Mott-like insulator Sr
[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032024] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: Investigates the relationship between local lattice distortions and electronic structure in the Mott insulator Sr2IrO4 using x-ray scattering, structural modeling, and DFT.
motivation: To understand how local lattice distortions affect the electronic band gap in a spin-orbit-coupled Mott insulator.

authors: Chu-Lun Chen, Chin-Hsuan Chen, And Horng-Tay Jeng
abstract:
Author(s): Chu-Lun Chen, Chin-Hsuan Chen, and Horng-Tay Jeng

FeGe is the only known kagome metal hosting the coexistence of long-range magnetic order and charge-density-wave (CDW) order, making it an exceptional platform for studying spin-charge-lattice entanglement. Despite extensive experimental and theoretical efforts, the microscopic origin of the CDW in …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033212] Published Thu Aug 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates strain-induced charge-density-wave phase transitions in the magnetic kagome metal FeGe, aiming to understand the microscopic origin of the coexisting CDW and magnetic order.
motivation: FeGe is unique among kagome metals in hosting both long-range magnetic order and CDW order, but the microscopic mechanism behind the CDW remains unclear. This work explores how strain can tune these competing orders to shed light on spin-charge-lattice coupling.
method: Using first-principles calculations, the study examines the effect of strain on the electronic structure and the relative stability of magnetic and CDW phases in FeGe.
result: The calculations identify specific strain conditions that can induce CDW phase transitions and alter the magnetic ground state, revealing a strong sensitivity of the phase stability to lattice distortions.
conclusion: Strain provides an effective control parameter for manipulating CDW and magnetic order in FeGe, which may help clarify the origin of CDW and the interplay between spin, charge, and lattice degrees of freedom in kagome systems.

title: Directional Hydraulic Stress Indices Predict Root Growth And Hormonal Reprogramming In Plants
authors: Kaushal Agarwal, Sumit Kumar Mehta, Amy Q. Shen, And Pranab Kumar Mondal
abstract:

Plants navigate fluctuating fluid environments in both soil and hydroponic systems, yet the physical principles by which roots transduce directional hydrodynamic forcing into developmental responses remain poorly quantified. By combining a flow-configurable microfluidic platform (P-ROOT) with fluid-…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033209] Published Wed Aug 19, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how directional hydraulic stress in microfluidic environments affects root growth and hormonal responses in plants.
motivation: To quantify the physical principles by which roots transduce directional hydrodynamic forcing into developmental responses, which remains poorly understood.
method: The authors use a flow-configurable microfluidic platform (P-ROOT) combined with fluid dynamics and hormonal analysis to expose roots to controlled hydraulic stresses.
result: They identify directional hydraulic stress indices that predict root growth patterns and correlate with hormonal reprogramming.
conclusion: The study provides quantitative links between fluid mechanics and plant developmental biology, offering insights into root adaptation in dynamic fluid environments.

title: Collective Chemotactic Search
authors: Adam Wysocki, Hugues Meyer, And Heiko Rieger
abstract:
