We investigate collective search by self-propelled agents that are repelled by their own chemically produced trails, a minimal mechanism that simultaneously generates indirect interactions and memory. Using lattice and off-lattice models, we show that this mechanism enhances search efficiency throug…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033201] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies collective search by self-propelled agents repelled by their own chemical trails, showing enhanced search efficiency via indirect interactions and memory.
motivation: To understand how minimal mechanisms involving chemical trails can improve collective search efficiency in active matter systems.
method: Uses lattice and off-lattice models to simulate self-propelled agents that repel each other via their own chemical trails, analyzing search efficiency.
result: The mechanism enhances search efficiency through collective effects and memory, as demonstrated in simulations.
conclusion: Repulsive chemotaxis is a simple and effective strategy for collective search, with potential applications in swarm robotics and biological systems.

title: Symmetric Preferences, Asymmetric Outcomes: Tipping Dynamics In An Open-city Segregation Model
authors: Fabio van Dissel, Tuan Minh Pham, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Fabio van Dissel, Tuan Minh Pham, and Wout Merbis

Schelling's model of segregation demonstrates that even in the absence of social or governmental interventions, individuals with mild in-group preferences can self-organize into strongly segregated neighborhoods. Many variants of this celebrated model have been proposed by assuming that agents tend …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033202] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies tipping dynamics in an open-city version of Schelling's segregation model, showing that symmetric preferences can lead to asymmetric segregation outcomes.
motivation: To understand how individual preferences, even when symmetric, can produce strongly segregated neighborhoods, especially in dynamic urban settings with population turnover.
method: The authors analyze an extension of Schelling's model where agents can move in and out of the city, focusing on the conditions that trigger rapid segregation transitions.
result: The model demonstrates that symmetric in-group preferences, combined with open-city dynamics, can result in asymmetric outcomes where one group dominates certain neighborhoods due to tipping points.
conclusion: The findings highlight the role of mobility and tipping dynamics in segregation, suggesting that policy interventions may need to address these mechanisms rather than just preferences.

title: Chaos Suppression Via Adaptive Feedback Control Of Intermittency
authors: Mohammad Yahyavi, Sina Gholizadeh, Sohrab Behnia, And Bilal Tanatar
abstract:
Author(s): Mohammad Yahyavi, Sina Gholizadeh, Sohrab Behnia, and Bilal Tanatar

Intermittency represents a fundamental route to chaos in nonlinear dynamical systems. In this work, we introduce an adaptive control strategy in which the control parameter of an intermittent system is promoted to a dynamical variable that evolves autonomously under an auxiliary nonlinear map drawn …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033205] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an adaptive feedback control method to suppress chaos via intermittency by promoting the control parameter to a dynamical variable.
motivation: Intermittency is a fundamental route to chaos, and controlling it is important for stabilizing nonlinear dynamical systems.
method: The control parameter is promoted to a dynamical variable evolving under an auxiliary nonlinear map, creating an adaptive feedback loop.
result: The method effectively suppresses chaos in intermittent systems, as demonstrated through analysis and simulations.
conclusion: Adaptive feedback control of intermittency provides a novel approach to chaos suppression in nonlinear systems.

title: From Delay To Inertia And Triadic Interactions: A Predictive Model For Time-delayed Oscillator Networks
authors: Lev A. Smirnov, Vyacheslav O. Munyayev, Maxim I. Bolotov, And Igor Belykh
abstract:

In this work, we develop a universal second-order predictive reduction for time-delayed Kuramoto-Daido networks tha…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033189] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: Develops a second-order predictive reduction for time-delayed Kuramoto-Daido oscillator networks to capture high-dimensional collective dynamics.
motivation: Standard first-order phase reductions fail to capture the high-dimensional collective dynamics of time-delayed oscillator networks.
method: Develops a universal second-order predictive reduction for time-delayed Kuramoto-Daido networks.
result: The reduction accurately predicts the collective dynamics of time-delayed oscillator networks.
conclusion: The second-order predictive reduction provides a better model for time-delayed oscillator networks.

title: Distinction Of Time-reversal-like Degeneracy By Electronic Transport In ${\mathrm{Ce}}_{3}{\mathrm{MgBi}}_{5}$

tldr: This paper reports the discovery of an antiferromagnetic compound Ce3MgBi5 with a distorted kagome lattice, revealing hidden time-reversal-like degenerate states via electronic transport measurements.
motivation: To identify and characterize emergent electronic states in a novel magnetic compound that may host exotic quantum phenomena such as fractional magnetization steps and degenerate band structures.
method: The authors performed electronic transport measurements (likely including resistivity and Hall effect) to probe the electronic structure and detect signatures of time-reversal-like degeneracy.
result: The measurements reveal fractional magnetization steps and evidence of hidden degenerate states, indicating nontrivial electronic behavior in the antiferromagnetic kagome lattice.
conclusion: The compound Ce3MgBi5 is a promising platform for studying correlated electron physics and potential topological properties, though its relevance to quantum information or quantum networks is not established.

title: Optical Observation Of Flat-band Charge Dynamics In Kagome Metal ${\mathrm{CsCr}}_{6}{\mathrm{Sb}}_{6}$
authors: Dongwook Kim, Boqin Song, Zhenzhen Xu, Sangjun Han, Tianping Ying, And S. J. Moon
abstract:

Flat-band systems, where electron kinetic energy is quenched over large regions of momentum space, are predicted to host exotic strongly correlated phenomena. Kagome metals have emerged as a prominent platform for exploring intriguing flat-band physics. Yet, their intrinsic charge dynamics have rema…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033183] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports optical observations of flat-band charge dynamics in the kagome metal CsCr6Sb6.
motivation: Flat-band systems are predicted to host exotic strongly correlated phenomena, and kagome metals are a prominent platform to study such physics. The intrinsic charge dynamics in these materials have remained unexplored, motivating this study.
method: The authors used optical spectroscopy measurements to probe the charge dynamics of CsCr6Sb6, likely measuring reflectivity or optical conductivity.
result: The observations reveal optical signatures associated with flat-band charge dynamics, providing direct evidence for the predicted flat-band physics.
conclusion: The findings contribute to understanding correlated phenomena in kagome metals and demonstrate the utility of optical methods in probing flat-band systems.

title: Spin-to-orbital Angular Momentum Conversion In non-Hermitian Photonic Graphene

Optical beams with orbital angular momentum (OAM) have numerous potential applications, but the means used for their generation often lack crucial on-demand control. In this work, we present a mechanism of converting spin angular momentum (SAM) to OAM in a nonstructured beam. The conversion occurs t…

tldr: This paper demonstrates a mechanism for converting spin angular momentum to orbital angular momentum in a non-structured beam using non-Hermitian photonic graphene.
motivation: OAM beams have numerous applications, but current generation methods often lack on-demand control. This work aims to provide a new conversion mechanism.
method: The authors utilize non-Hermitian photonic graphene structures to facilitate the SAM-to-OAM conversion without requiring a structured beam.
result: The conversion occurs effectively in a non-structured beam, offering a new approach to generate OAM.
conclusion: The proposed mechanism enables controllable SAM-to-OAM conversion, potentially advancing applications in optical manipulation and communications.

authors: Shizhen Zhi, Xiaojing Ma, Shanghao Chen, Tianyu Zhang, Yao Xu, Jiang Chen, Sheng Ye, Chenhao Lin, Linmao Wen, Jinxuan Cheng, Rongpei Shi, Xingjun Liu, Feng Cao, Lijun Zhang, Yuhao Fu, Qian Zhang, And Jun Mao

title: Strain-Tunable Anomalous Hall Effect In Hexagonal MnTe
authors: Zhaoyu Liu, Sijie Xu, Jonathan M. Destefano, Elliott Rosenberg, Tingjun Zhang, Jinyulin Li, Matthew B. Stone, Feng Ye, Wei Tian, Sarah Edwards, Rong Cong, Siyu Pan, Ching-Wu Chu, Liangzi Deng, Emilia Morosan, Rafael M. Fernandes, Jiun-Haw Chu, And Pengcheng Dai

Uniaxial strain applied to the hexagonal altermagnet
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031033] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the strain-tunable anomalous Hall effect in hexagonal MnTe, an altermagnet, and finds that uniaxial strain isolates a single magnetic domain and causes a sign reversal of the Hall effect due to Berry curvature modifications.
motivation: To understand and control the anomalous Hall effect in altermagnets, which is of interest for spintronic applications.
method: Apply uniaxial strain to hexagonal MnTe and measure the anomalous Hall effect; analyze changes in magnetic domain structure and electronic Berry curvature.
result: Uniaxial strain isolates a single magnetic domain, producing a sharp anomalous Hall effect and a sign reversal driven by Berry curvature modifications.
conclusion: Strain is an effective knob to control the anomalous Hall effect in altermagnets, with potential implications for spintronics.

authors: Nina Javerzat And Daniele Notarmuzi

method: Resonant inelastic x-ray scattering (RIXS) measurements were performed on a low-valence nickelate compound to probe its electronic excitations.
result: Propagating plasmons were observed with dynamics that differ significantly from those in cuprate superconductors.
conclusion: The distinct plasmon behavior in nickelates provides new insights into the correlated electron physics of these materials, which may be relevant for understanding high-temperature superconductivity.

method: Presumably uses theoretical analysis and/or numerical simulations of network models to compare structural and dynamical dimensions.
result: Finds that low-dimensional network structures can lead to both high- and low-dimensional dynamics, indicating a non-trivial mapping.
conclusion: The dimensionality of network dynamics is not solely determined by structural dimensionality, with implications for understanding complex systems.

title: Evaporative Flux Reversal Of Binary Droplets: From Edge To Apex

Experimental studies of multicomponent droplet evaporation reveal distinct stages, with internal flow shifting from multiple vortices within the droplet to a single toroidal vortex dominating the flow dynamic, departing from the classical single-component picture.

title: Evidence Of Nuclear Geometry-Driven Anisotropic Flow In $\mathrm{O}+\mathrm{O}$ And $\mathrm{Ne}+\mathrm{Ne}$ Collisions At $\sqrt{{s}_{\mathrm{NN}}}=5.36\text{ }\text{ }\mathrm{TeV}$
authors: I. J. Abualrob et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): I. J. Abualrob et al. (ALICE Collaboration)

[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 082301] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports measurements of anisotropic flow in O+O and Ne+Ne collisions at LHC energies, showing a larger elliptic flow in Ne+Ne that may be attributed to the deformed 'bowling-pin' shape of neon nuclei.
motivation: To investigate whether nuclear geometry and deformation affect collective flow in small collision systems, providing new insights into the onset of hydrodynamic behavior.
method: Analysis of ALICE data for O+O and Ne+Ne collisions at sqrt(s_NN)=5.36 TeV, focusing on the elliptic flow coefficient as a function of centrality.
result: A larger elliptic flow is observed in central Ne+Ne collisions compared to O+O, consistent with the expected influence of the prolate (bowling-pin) deformation of neon.
conclusion: The measurement provides evidence that nuclear shape drives anisotropic flow in light-ion collisions, highlighting the role of initial geometry in small systems.
